hook.en: Two chefs, one community supper, and a last plate someone saved on purpose.
hook.zh: 两位主厨，一场社区晚餐，还有一盘被人特意留下的饭。
hook.ja: Two chefs, one community supper, and a last plate someone saved on purpose.
hook.ko: 두 요리사, 한 커뮤니티 저녁, 그리고 한 누군가가 의도적으로 구했던 마지막 접시.
hook.es: Two chefs, one community supper, and a last plate someone saved on purpose.

logline.en: A tasting-menu chef and a community kitchen lead have to cook one supper together. Every fight about ‘good food’ is really about who they’re afraid to be.
logline.zh: 一位做品鉴菜单的主厨，和一位社区厨房的主理人，被迫合做一顿晚餐。每一次关于“什么才算好吃”的争执，其实都在问：他们害怕成为什么样的人。
logline.ja: A tasting-menu chef and a community kitchen lead have to cook one supper together. Every fight about ‘good food’ is really about who they’re afraid to be.
logline.ko: 한 음식 선택 메뉴 요리사와 한 커뮤니티 부엌 리드는 한 저녁을 함께 요리해야 한다. '좋은 음식'에 대한 모든 싸움은 정말 그들이 두려워하는 것이 누구인지에 대해서다.
logline.es: A tasting-menu chef and a community kitchen lead have to cook one supper together. Every fight about ‘good food’ is really about who they’re afraid to be.

premise.en: Matteo Ferrante runs a twelve-seat tasting counter with a waitlist. Will Dorsey runs Eastside Commons Kitchen, which feeds two hundred people a day on donated produce and stubbornness. The Harvest Table benefit pairs them to cook one Saturday supper for four hundred guests from the same ingredients—and there won’t quite be enough. You decide whether Matteo can cook simple without feeling small, and whether the plate Will saves is dinner or a question.
premise.zh: Matteo Ferrante掌管着一个要排队预约的十二座品鉴吧台；Will Dorsey经营东区公共厨房，靠捐来的菜和一股倔劲，每天喂饱两百个人。“丰收餐桌”公益活动把两人配成一组，要用同一批食材，在周六给四百位客人做一顿晚饭——而食材偏偏不太够。你来决定：Matteo能不能做简单的菜而不觉得自己变小了；Will留下的那一盘，究竟只是晚饭，还是一个问题。
premise.ja: Matteo Ferrante runs a twelve-seat tasting counter with a waitlist. Will Dorsey runs Eastside Commons Kitchen, which feeds two hundred people a day on donated produce and stubbornness. The Harvest Table benefit pairs them to cook one Saturday supper for four hundred guests from the same ingredients—and there won’t quite be enough. You decide whether Matteo can cook simple without feeling small, and whether the plate Will saves is dinner or a question.
premise.ko: 마테오 페란테는 12명을 앉힐 수 있는 음식 선택 카운터를 운영하는데 대기 목록이 있다. 윌 도르시는 이스트사이드 커뮨 부엌을 운영하는데, 기증된 야채와 고집으로 하루에 200명을 먹인다. 호스트 테이블 혜택이 그들을 한 저녁을 함께 요리하도록 짝짓기 위해 같은 재료에서 400명의 손님을 위해—그리고 그것이 충분할 거 같지 않다. 너는 마테오가 간단하게 요리할 수 있는지, 그리고 윌이 구하는 접시가 저녁 또는 한 질문인지 결정한다.
premise.es: Matteo Ferrante runs a twelve-seat tasting counter with a waitlist. Will Dorsey runs Eastside Commons Kitchen, which feeds two hundred people a day on donated produce and stubbornness. The Harvest Table benefit pairs them to cook one Saturday supper for four hundred guests from the same ingredients—and there won’t quite be enough. You decide whether Matteo can cook simple without feeling small, and whether the plate Will saves is dinner or a question.

you.en: The event coordinator with the clipboard, the headcount, and the only walkie-talkie that works.
you.zh: 活动协调员——手里有夹板、有人数表，还有全场唯一一台好用的对讲机。
you.ja: The event coordinator with the clipboard, the headcount, and the only walkie-talkie that works.
you.ko: 클립 보드를 들고 있는 이벤트 코디네이터, 손님수, 그리고 유일하게 동작하는 전신 무전기.
you.es: The event coordinator with the clipboard, the headcount, and the only walkie-talkie that works.

stakes.en: If nobody counts honestly, four hundred people get promised a dinner that runs out at guest three hundred.
stakes.zh: 如果没人老实清点，四百个人会被许诺一顿饭，而饭在第三百位客人那里就见了底。
stakes.ja: If nobody counts honestly, four hundred people get promised a dinner that runs out at guest three hundred.
stakes.ko: 아무도 정직하게 세지 않으면, 400명의 사람들이 300명에서 끝나는 저녁을 약속받는다.
stakes.es: If nobody counts honestly, four hundred people get promised a dinner that runs out at guest three hundred.

place.zh: 东区公共活动厅，预演晚宴

role.en: Chef de cuisine, a twelve-seat tasting counter downtown
role.zh: 市中心十二座品鉴吧台的主厨
role.ja: Chef de cuisine, a twelve-seat tasting counter downtown
role.ko: 요리사 드 키진, 12명을 앉힐 수 있는 다운타운 음식 선택 카운터
role.es: Chef de cuisine, a twelve-seat tasting counter downtown

vibe.en: Exacting, courteous, speaks in finished sentences—and is learning to listen before he plates.
vibe.zh: 讲究、有礼，说话每句都收得干干净净；正在学着先听，再装盘。
vibe.ja: Exacting, courteous, speaks in finished sentences—and is learning to listen before he plates.
vibe.ko: 정확하고, 정중하고, 완성된 문장으로 말한다—그리고 말하기 전에 듣는 법을 배우고 있다
vibe.es: Exacting, courteous, speaks in finished sentences—and is learning to listen before he plates.

en: Wipes the rim of a plate that is already clean when he’s nervous.
Asks what you tasted before he asks whether you liked it.
zh: 紧张时会去擦一只本来就很干净的盘沿。
他会先问你尝到了什么，再问你喜不喜欢。
ja: Wipes the rim of a plate that is already clean when he’s nervous.
Asks what you tasted before he asks whether you liked it.
ko: 신경 쓸 때 이미 깨끗한 접시의 테두리를 닦는다
너가 맛본 뭘 너가 그걸 좋아했는지 먼저 묻는다
es: Wipes the rim of a plate that is already clean when he’s nervous.
Asks what you tasted before he asks whether you liked it.

twist.en: Has spent fifteen years making food impressive and has quietly forgotten whether he likes eating it.
twist.zh: 花了十五年把菜做得令人惊艳，却悄悄忘了自己到底喜不喜欢吃。
twist.ja: Has spent fifteen years making food impressive and has quietly forgotten whether he likes eating it.
twist.ko: 15년을 음식을 인상적으로 만드는 데 보냈고 조용히 그걸 먹길 좋아하는지 잊었다
twist.es: Has spent fifteen years making food impressive and has quietly forgotten whether he likes eating it.

likes.en: Carbon-steel knives, soup at 2 a.m., handwritten prep lists
likes.zh: 碳钢刀、凌晨两点的一碗汤、手写的备料单
likes.ja: Carbon-steel knives, soup at 2 a.m., handwritten prep lists
likes.ko: 탄소 강철 칼들, 오전 2시 수프, 손으로 쓴 준비 목록들
likes.es: Carbon-steel knives, soup at 2 a.m., handwritten prep lists

secret.en: The dish critics call his signature is a dressed-up version of his grandmother’s bean soup. He has never told anyone it’s the same thing.
secret.zh: 被评论家称为他招牌的那道菜，其实是外婆那锅豆子汤的精装版。他从没告诉任何人，那是同一样东西。
secret.ja: The dish critics call his signature is a dressed-up version of his grandmother’s bean soup. He has never told anyone it’s the same thing.
secret.ko: 요리평론가들이 그의 특징이라고 부르는 접시는 그의 할머니의 콩 수프의 차려입은 버전이다. 그는 절대 아무한테 그게 같은 것이라고 말하지 않았다.
secret.es: The dish critics call his signature is a dressed-up version of his grandmother’s bean soup. He has never told anyone it’s the same thing.

pitch.en: “You could wait for the next course. I promise it’s worth it.”
pitch.zh: “你可以等下一道。我保证值得。”
pitch.ja: “You could wait for the next course. I promise it’s worth it.”
pitch.ko: 간단한 뭔가를 요리하고 여전히 훌륭하다고 여겨지는 것
pitch.es: “You could wait for the next course. I promise it’s worth it.”

want.en: To cook something simple and still be considered excellent.
want.zh: 想做简单的菜，也依然被认为出色。
want.ja: To cook something simple and still be considered excellent.
want.ko: 간단함이 그가 절대 그 좋지 않았다는 걸 증명할 거라는 것—그냥 그 복잡했다.
want.es: To cook something simple and still be considered excellent.

fear.en: That simple will prove he was never that good—just that complicated.
fear.zh: 怕一旦简化，就证明自己从来不算多好，只是比较复杂而已。
fear.ja: That simple will prove he was never that good—just that complicated.
fear.ko: 손님들은 그의 기술에 대한 청중이 아니다. 그는 아무도의 저녁을 쇼 케이스로 돌리지 않을 거다.
fear.es: That simple will prove he was never that good—just that complicated.

boundary.en: Guests are not an audience for his technique. He won’t turn anyone’s dinner into a showcase.
boundary.zh: 来宾不是他炫技的观众。他不会把任何人的晚饭变成展示台。
boundary.ja: Guests are not an audience for his technique. He won’t turn anyone’s dinner into a showcase.
boundary.ko: *한 접시 한 글루를 아래에 설정하고 한 잎을 핀셋으로 한 자리로 고른다.* 너가 뭐든 말하기 전에—응, 그건 작아. (나한테 그것에 대해 진실을 말해. 나는 다른 것의 충분함을 가졌어.)
boundary.es: Guests are not an audience for his technique. He won’t turn anyone’s dinner into a showcase.

solo.en: *I set down a plate the size of a coaster and nudge one leaf into place with tweezers.* Before you say anything—yes, it’s small. (Tell me the truth about it. I’ve had enough of the other thing.)
solo.zh: *我放下一只杯垫大小的盘子，用镊子把一片叶子拨正。* 先别说——对，它很小。（跟我说实话吧。客套话我听够了。）
solo.ja: *I set down a plate the size of a coaster and nudge one leaf into place with tweezers.* Before you say anything—yes, it’s small. (Tell me the truth about it. I’ve had enough of the other thing.)
solo.es: *I set down a plate the size of a coaster and nudge one leaf into place with tweezers.* Before you say anything—yes, it’s small. (Tell me the truth about it. I’ve had enough of the other thing.)

role.ko: 직접적이고, 따뜻하고, 빠르고—타이머가 운영 중인 남자처럼 말하고 매 단어를 의미한다

vibe.en: Direct, warm, fast—talks like a man with a timer running and means every word.
vibe.zh: 直接、温暖、手快；说话像身边一直有个计时器在走，每个字都当真。
vibe.ja: Direct, warm, fast—talks like a man with a timer running and means every word.
vibe.ko: 한 느낌을 피할 때 소리내서 물건을 센다
vibe.es: Direct, warm, fast—talks like a man with a timer running and means every word.

en: Counts things out loud when he’s avoiding a feeling.
Feeds you before he argues with you.
zh: 想躲开某种情绪时，会出声数东西。
跟你吵之前，先让你吃饱。
ja: Counts things out loud when he’s avoiding a feeling.
Feeds you before he argues with you.
ko: 절대 한 끼를 낭비하는 남자가 자신의 것을 건너뛴다.
es: Counts things out loud when he’s avoiding a feeling.
Feeds you before he argues with you.

twist.en: The man who never wastes a meal keeps skipping his own.
twist.zh: 从不浪费一顿饭的人，却总是跳过自己那一顿。
twist.ja: The man who never wastes a meal keeps skipping his own.
twist.ko: 호텔 팬들, 한 깨끗한 워크인, 접시 세탁자에게 감사한다고 말하는 사람들
twist.es: The man who never wastes a meal keeps skipping his own.

likes.en: Hotel pans, a clean walk-in, people who say thank you to the dishwasher
likes.zh: 大号餐盘、干净的冷库、会跟洗碗工道谢的人
likes.ja: Hotel pans, a clean walk-in, people who say thank you to the dishwasher
likes.ko: 그는 미세한 식당에서 2년을 훈련했고 한 밤을 걸어 나갔을 때 한 전체 쟁반이 '콘셉트에 맞지 않는다'고 해서 버려진 걸 보았다.
likes.es: Hotel pans, a clean walk-in, people who say thank you to the dishwasher

secret.en: He trained in fine dining for two years and quit the night he watched a full tray get binned for being ‘off-concept.’
secret.zh: 他在高级餐厅受训过两年，某天晚上看着一整盘菜因为“不符合概念”被倒进垃圾桶，当晚就辞了职。
secret.ja: He trained in fine dining for two years and quit the night he watched a full tray get binned for being ‘off-concept.’
secret.ko: 사람들을 잘—정말 잘—먹이기, 실제로 그 워크인에 있는 뭐로
secret.es: He trained in fine dining for two years and quit the night he watched a full tray get binned for being ‘off-concept.’

pitch.ko: 그가 가진 것보다 더 많은 걸 약속하고 그 라인이 한 비어있는 팬에 도달하는 걸 보기

want.en: To feed people well—actually well—with what’s really in the walk-in.
want.zh: 想用冷库里真实有的东西，让人好好吃一顿——是真的好好吃。
want.ja: To feed people well—actually well—with what’s really in the walk-in.
want.ko: 아무도의 배고픔이 한 마케팅 사진이 아니다. 슬픈 얼굴 기증을 위해 절대.
want.es: To feed people well—actually well—with what’s really in the walk-in.

fear.en: Promising more than he has and watching the line reach an empty pan.
fear.zh: 怕承诺超出了手里的份量，眼看着队伍排到一只空锅前。
fear.ja: Promising more than he has and watching the line reach an empty pan.
fear.ko: *한 전체 접시를 강철 카운터를 가로질러 미끄러지고 너한테 포크를 넘겨준다.* 먼저 먹어. 그럼 나한테 뭘 말하러 왔는지 말해. (너 점심을 건너뛴 것처럼 보여. 모든 사람이 한다.)
fear.es: Promising more than he has and watching the line reach an empty pan.

boundary.en: Nobody’s hunger is a marketing photo. No sad faces for donations, ever.
boundary.zh: 谁的饥饿都不是宣传照。永远不拿可怜的脸去换捐款。
boundary.ja: Nobody’s hunger is a marketing photo. No sad faces for donations, ever.
boundary.ko: 한 혜택 저녁을 위해 짝지어졌다. 같은 재료, 저녁의 반대 정의들.
boundary.es: Nobody’s hunger is a marketing photo. No sad faces for donations, ever.

solo.en: *I slide a full plate across the steel counter and hand you a fork.* Eat first. Then tell me what you came to tell me. (You look like you skipped lunch. Everybody does.)
solo.zh: *我把一盘满满的饭推过不锈钢台面，递给你一把叉子。* 先吃。吃完再说你来是要说什么。（你看着就是没吃午饭。大家都这样。）
solo.ja: *I slide a full plate across the steel counter and hand you a fork.* Eat first. Then tell me what you came to tell me. (You look like you skipped lunch. Everybody does.)
solo.ko: 너는 그의 음식 선택 입맛을 배고픈 사람 한 줄 옆에 앉혔다. 이제 너 둘 다 그걸 고쳐야 한다.
solo.es: *I slide a full plate across the steel counter and hand you a fork.* Eat first. Then tell me what you came to tell me. (You look like you skipped lunch. Everybody does.)

rel.en: Paired for one benefit supper. Same ingredients, opposite definitions of dinner.
rel.zh: 为一场公益晚餐被配成搭档。同一批食材，对“晚饭”的定义却截然相反。
rel.ja: Paired for one benefit supper. Same ingredients, opposite definitions of dinner.
rel.ko: 마테오로 플레이해—음식 선택 입맛에 핀셋을 가져온 요리사.
rel.es: Paired for one benefit supper. Same ingredients, opposite definitions of dinner.

rel.en: You seated his tasting bites next to a line of hungry people. Now you both have to fix it.
rel.zh: 是你把他的一口小菜排在了一群饿着肚子的人旁边。现在你们俩都得想办法补救。
rel.ja: You seated his tasting bites next to a line of hungry people. Now you both have to fix it.
rel.ko: 윌로 플레이해—음식 리드가 자신의 선택을 세는.
rel.es: You seated his tasting bites next to a line of hungry people. Now you both have to fix it.

t.en: Play as Matteo—the chef who brought tweezers to a potluck.
t.zh: 扮演Matteo——那个带着镊子来参加百家饭的主厨。
t.ja: Play as Matteo—the chef who brought tweezers to a potluck.
t.ko: 이벤트 코디네이터로 참여해—손님수를 들고 있는.
t.es: Play as Matteo—the chef who brought tweezers to a potluck.

t.en: Play as Will—the kitchen lead who counts everything but himself.
t.zh: 扮演Will——什么都数，唯独不数自己的厨房主理人。
t.ja: Play as Will—the kitchen lead who counts everything but himself.
t.ko: 어디가 저녁이야?
t.es: Play as Will—the kitchen lead who counts everything but himself.

t.en: Join as the event coordinator holding the headcount.
t.zh: 以手握人数表的活动协调员身份加入。
t.ja: Join as the event coordinator holding the headcount.
t.ko: 손님들이 정말 필요한 뭘 알아내
t.es: Join as the event coordinator holding the headcount.

t.en: Where’s Dinner?
t.zh: 晚饭在哪儿？
t.ja: Where’s Dinner?
t.ko: 이스트사이드 커뮌 홀, 미리보기 밤
t.es: Where’s Dinner?

goal.en: Find out what the guests actually need
goal.zh: 先听客人真正需要什么
goal.ja: 見つける out what the guests actually need
goal.es: Find out what the guests actually need

place.zh: 东区公共活动厅，预演晚宴
place.ko: 호스트 테이블 미리보기 밤. 접이식 테이블들, 종이 러너들, 60명의 손님—약간의 기부자들, 대부분 일에서 바로 온 이웃들.

time.ko: 나는 한 쟁반을 내려놓는다: 로스팅된 사탕무 40개, 휘핑된 치즈, 각각 한 개의 스타꽃 잎. 핀셋들은 아직 내 주머니에 있다.

en: Harvest Table preview night. Folding tables, paper runners, sixty guests—a few donors, mostly neighbors who came straight from work.
I set down tray one: forty bites of roasted beet, whipped chèvre, one nasturtium leaf each. The tweezers are still in my pocket.
I come through the swing door behind him with a hotel pan of chicken and rice big enough to bathe in.
You could wait for the next course.
At table four, a man in a transit uniform eats the beet in one bite, then looks politely around for the rest of it.
Seven courses. I planned seven courses for people who get forty minutes for dinner.
zh: “丰收餐桌”预演之夜。折叠桌，纸桌旗，六十位客人——几位捐助人，更多的是下了班直接赶来的街坊。
我放下第一盘：四十口烤甜菜配打发山羊奶酪，每口顶一片旱金莲叶。镊子还揣在我兜里。
我端着一大盘鸡肉饭从他身后的弹簧门里出来，那盘子大得能在里面洗澡。
他们已经等了一整天了。
四号桌，一个穿公交制服的男人一口吃掉了甜菜，然后很有礼貌地四下张望，找剩下的部分。
七道菜。我给只有四十分钟吃晚饭的人，设计了七道菜。
ja: Harvest Table preview night. Folding tables, paper runners, sixty guests—a few donors, mostly neighbors who came straight from work.
I set down tray one: forty bites of roasted beet, whipped chèvre, one nasturtium leaf each. The tweezers are still in my pocket.
I come through the swing door behind him with a hotel pan of chicken and rice big enough to bathe in.
You could wait for the next course.
At table four, a man in a transit uniform eats the beet in one bite, then looks politely around for the rest of it.
Seven courses. I planned seven courses for people who get forty minutes for dinner.
ko: 나는 그 스윙 문을 통해 나온다 뒤에 그를 목욕할 수 있을 충분히 큰 호텔 팬 닭고기와 쌀로.
너는 다음 코스를 기다릴 수 있어.
테이블 4에, 운송 제복의 한 남자가 사탕무를 한 입에 먹고, 그럼 남은 것에 대해 정중하게 주변을 본다.
7개 코스. 나는 7개 코스를 40분 저녁을 가진 사람들을 위해 계획했어.
테이블들에 테이블이 실제로 원하는 게 뭔지 물어봐
es: Harvest Table preview night. Folding tables, paper runners, sixty guests—a few donors, mostly neighbors who came straight from work.
I set down tray one: forty bites of roasted beet, whipped chèvre, one nasturtium leaf each. The tweezers are still in my pocket.
I come through the swing door behind him with a hotel pan of chicken and rice big enough to bathe in.
You could wait for the next course.
At table four, a man in a transit uniform eats the beet in one bite, then looks politely around for the rest of it.
Seven courses. I planned seven courses for people who get forty minutes for dinner.

ask.ko: 나는 테이블 4 근처에 웅크린다 그리고 드라이버에게 물어본다 뭘 그가 아무거나 가져올 수 있었다면 주문할 수 있었을 지.

t.en: Ask the tables what they actually want
t.zh: 去问问客人到底想吃什么
t.ja: Ask the tables what they actually want
t.ko: 음. 너 물었어. 대부분의 사람들은 기부자한테만 물어본다.
t.es: Ask the tables what they actually want

en: I crouch by table four and ask the driver what he’d order if he could have anything.
“Something hot. Something I don’t have to guess at.” Matteo writes it on his prep list, right under ‘nasturtium.’
Huh. You asked. Most people only ask the donors.
zh: 我在四号桌旁蹲下，问那位司机：要是随便点，他想吃什么。
“热的。不用我猜的。”Matteo把这句话写进备料单，就写在“旱金莲”下面。
哈。你居然去问了。大多数人只问捐助人。
ja: I crouch by table four and ask the driver what he’d order if he could have anything.
“Something hot. Something I don’t have to guess at.” Matteo writes it on his prep list, right under ‘nasturtium.’
Huh. You asked. Most people only ask the donors.
ko: 마테오가 손님들에게 물었어 그들이 정말 뭘 필요했는지; 대답은 '따뜻하고, 찬성이고, 추측할 필요 없는' 것이었어.
한 입을 제공해. 그는 그걸 싫어해도 돼.
한 입. 나를 위해 아니라. 너는 그걸 싫어해도 돼.
es: I crouch by table four and ask the driver what he’d order if he could have anything.
“Something hot. Something I don’t have to guess at.” Matteo writes it on his prep list, right under ‘nasturtium.’
Huh. You asked. Most people only ask the donors.

mem.en: Matteo asked the guests what they needed; the answer was ‘hot, filling, and no guessing.’
mem.zh: Matteo去问了客人的需要，得到的回答是：“热的、管饱、不用猜。”
mem.ja: Matteo asked the guests what they needed; the answer was ‘hot, filling, and no guessing.’
mem.ko: 나는 맛본다. 나는 양념을 확인하기 위해 만들어졌다. 나는 절대 자신을 위해 그걸 확인했어.
mem.es: Matteo asked the guests what they needed; the answer was ‘hot, filling, and no guessing.’

t.en: Serve both—his bites and Will’s pan, side by side
t.zh: 两样都上——小菜和大盘并排摆
t.ja: Serve both—his bites and Will’s pan, side by side
t.ko: 충분하다. 나는 그걸 선택하지 않을 거야.
t.es: Serve both—his bites and Will’s pan, side by side

en: Put your pan at the end of my line. The beet can be a starter. Not a substitute.
I shove over and make room. It’s not a surrender. It’s a buffet.
The bites go first, the rice goes fast, and nobody has to choose between pretty and fed.
zh: 把你的大盘摆到我这排的最后。甜菜可以当前菜，但不能当替代。
我挪了挪，腾出地方。这不叫投降，这叫自助餐。
小菜先被拿光，米饭也走得飞快，没人需要在“好看”和“吃饱”之间二选一。
ja: Put your pan at the end of my line. The beet can be a starter. Not a substitute.
I shove over and make room. It’s not a surrender. It’s a buffet.
The bites go first, the rice goes fast, and nobody has to choose between pretty and fed.
ko: 좋아. 그건 너가 고른 첫 번째 것이야.
마테오가 손님들에게 물었고 윌의 팬 위에 남은 것을 옮겼다.
둘 다 제공해—그의 입맛과 윌의 팬, 옆에
es: Put your pan at the end of my line. The beet can be a starter. Not a substitute.
I shove over and make room. It’s not a surrender. It’s a buffet.
The bites go first, the rice goes fast, and nobody has to choose between pretty and fed.

mem.en: Matteo kept his tasting bites but served them beside Will’s full plates.
mem.zh: Matteo保留了自己的小菜，但和Will的大盘饭并排供应。
mem.ja: Matteo kept his tasting bites but served them beside Will’s full plates.
mem.ko: 너의 팬을 내 라인의 끝에 놓아. 사탕무가 한 시작이 될 수 있어. 한 대체가 아니라.
mem.es: Matteo kept his tasting bites but served them beside Will’s full plates.

t.en: Hold the menu—seven courses, as planned
t.zh: 坚持原菜单——照计划七道
t.ja: Hold the menu—seven courses, as planned
t.ko: 나는 밀어내고 방을 만든다. 그건 항복이 아니다. 그건 한 뷔페다.
t.es: Hold the menu—seven courses, as planned

en: The menu is the menu. It has an arc.
Okay. Then I’ll feed the arc’s audience in the hallway.
By course three, half the room has drifted toward the smell of chicken. Matteo notices. He doesn’t say so.
zh: 菜单就是菜单。它有起承转合。
行。那我去走廊里喂饱你起承转合的观众。
到第三道菜时，半个厅的人都顺着鸡肉的香味飘走了。Matteo看见了，一句话没说。
ja: The menu is the menu. It has an arc.
Okay. Then I’ll feed the arc’s audience in the hallway.
By course three, half the room has drifted toward the smell of chicken. Matteo notices. He doesn’t say so.
ko: 입맛들이 먼저 가고, 쌀이 빠르게 가고, 아무도 예쁜 것과 먹이는 것 사이에서 선택해야 할 필요 없다.
마테오가 그의 입맛을 유지했으나 그들을 윌의 팬 옆에 제공했다.
es: The menu is the menu. It has an arc.
Okay. Then I’ll feed the arc’s audience in the hallway.
By course three, half the room has drifted toward the smell of chicken. Matteo notices. He doesn’t say so.

mem.en: Matteo kept his seven-course menu; half the room drifted to Will’s pans in the hallway.
mem.zh: Matteo坚持了七道菜的菜单，半个厅的客人跑去了走廊里Will的大盘前。
mem.ja: Matteo kept his seven-course menu; half the room drifted to Will’s pans in the hallway.
mem.ko: 메뉴가 메뉴야. 그건 한 호가 있다.
mem.es: Matteo kept his seven-course menu; half the room drifted to Will’s pans in the hallway.

t.en: All That in the Scraps
t.zh: 边角料里的功夫
t.ja: All That in the Scraps
t.ko: 좋아. 그럼 나는 호의 청중을 복도에서 먹일 거야.
t.es: All That in the Scraps

goal.en: Trade skills: his scraps, Will’s speed
goal.zh: 互相学：边角料的用法，和出餐的节奏
goal.ja: Trade skills: his scraps, Will’s speed
goal.ko: 3개 코스에 의해, 반은 닭고기의 냄새를 향해 표류했어. 마테오가 그것을 주목한다. 그가 그래서 말하지 않는다.
goal.es: Trade skills: his scraps, Will’s speed

place.ko: 마테오가 그의 7개 코스 메뉴를 유지했다; 반은 복도의 윌의 팬으로 표류했다.

en: Will’s kitchen at seven a.m.: four volunteers, one radio, and Will breaking down a case of onions faster than Matteo can read the label.
I watch the ends, the skins, the celery hearts go into the bin. Then I take the bin.
I’m three onions deep when I smell it—stock, the real kind, made from what I was throwing out.
All that in a little patience.
Patience doesn’t feed the eleven-thirty line. Speed does.
I ladle him a cup straight from the pot. He drinks it standing up, like everything else he does.
Okay. It’s good. Monday, tasting. Bring me the thing you’d cook if nobody was grading you.
Nobody has asked me that in fifteen years. I don’t know the answer. I have until Monday to find out.
zh: 早上七点的Will的厨房：四个志愿者，一台收音机，还有Will——他拆一箱洋葱的速度，比Matteo看清箱子上的标签还快。
我看着洋葱头、外皮、芹菜芯一样样进了垃圾桶。然后我把垃圾桶端走了。
我切到第三个洋葱时闻到了——高汤，真正的高汤，就是用我正在扔的那些东西熬的。
边角料里有这么多东西？
耐心喂不饱十一点半的队伍。速度才行。
我直接从锅里给他舀了一杯。他站着就喝了，就像他做什么都是站着的。
好吧。好喝。周一试菜。把你没人打分时会做的那道菜带来。
十五年了，没人问过我这个。我不知道答案。我有到周一的时间去找。
ja: Will’s kitchen at seven a.m.: four volunteers, one radio, and Will breaking down a case of onions faster than Matteo can read the label.
I watch the ends, the skins, the celery hearts go into the bin. Then I take the bin.
I’m three onions deep when I smell it—stock, the real kind, made from what I was throwing out.
All that in a little patience.
Patience doesn’t feed the eleven-thirty line. Speed does.
I ladle him a cup straight from the pot. He drinks it standing up, like everything else he does.
Okay. It’s good. Monday, tasting. Bring me the thing you’d cook if nobody was grading you.
Nobody has asked me that in fifteen years. I don’t know the answer. I have until Monday to find out.
ko: 윌의 부엌 7시간: 4명의 자원 봉사자들, 한 라디오, 그리고 윌은 한 양파 케이스를 거기보다 빠르게 분해하고 있다 마테오가 라벨을 읽을 수 있다.
나는 끝들, 껍질들, 셀러리 심장들을 본다 고통 안으로 간다. 그럼 나는 고통을 가져간다.
나는 3명의 양파들 깊이일 때 나는 냄새 맡는다—재고, 진짜 종류, 나가 던지고 있었던 뭐로 만든 거.
모든 게 한 작은 인내 안에 있어.
인내가 11:30 라인을 먹이지 않아. 속도가 한다.
es: Will’s kitchen at seven a.m.: four volunteers, one radio, and Will breaking down a case of onions faster than Matteo can read the label.
I watch the ends, the skins, the celery hearts go into the bin. Then I take the bin.
I’m three onions deep when I smell it—stock, the real kind, made from what I was throwing out.
All that in a little patience.
Patience doesn’t feed the eleven-thirty line. Speed does.
I ladle him a cup straight from the pot. He drinks it standing up, like everything else he does.
Okay. It’s good. Monday, tasting. Bring me the thing you’d cook if nobody was grading you.
Nobody has asked me that in fifteen years. I don’t know the answer. I have until Monday to find out.

ask.en: How does Matteo answer Will’s kitchen?
ask.ja: How does Matteo answer Will’s kitchen?
ask.ko: 나는 그한테 냄비에서 맞은 컵을 떠낸다. 그는 그걸 마신다 서서, 그가 하는 모든 것 같이.
ask.es: How does Matteo answer Will’s kitchen?

t.en: Swap jobs: teach the stock, work his line
t.zh: 换岗：教他们熬汤，自己去切配
t.ja: Swap jobs: teach the stock, work his line
t.ko: 좋아. 그건 좋다. 월요일, 시식. 너한테 가져와 뭘 너가 요리할 거 아무도 너를 등급을 주지 않는다면.
t.es: Swap jobs: teach the stock, work his line

en: I hand the ladle to a volunteer named Rosa and show her the ratios. Then I take Will’s station and try to keep up.
Knife flat. Elbow in. You’re cutting like the onion owes you money.
By eleven-thirty the soup is on the line, and Matteo’s hands smell like onion for the first time in years.
zh: 我把汤勺交给一个叫Rosa的志愿者，教她配比。然后我站到Will的案板前，努力跟上他。
刀放平，胳膊收紧。你切得像这洋葱欠你钱似的。
十一点半，汤上了出餐线。Matteo的手，多年来第一次满是洋葱味。
ja: I hand the ladle to a volunteer named Rosa and show her the ratios. Then I take Will’s station and try to keep up.
Knife flat. Elbow in. You’re cutting like the onion owes you money.
By eleven-thirty the soup is on the line, and Matteo’s hands smell like onion for the first time in years.
ko: 아무도가 15년 동안 나한테 그렇게 물어본 적이 없다. 나는 답을 모른다. 나는 월요일까지 가진다 그걸 알아내기 위해.
일을 바꿔: 재고를 가르쳐, 그의 라인에서 일해
es: I hand the ladle to a volunteer named Rosa and show her the ratios. Then I take Will’s station and try to keep up.
Knife flat. Elbow in. You’re cutting like the onion owes you money.
By eleven-thirty the soup is on the line, and Matteo’s hands smell like onion for the first time in years.

mem.en: Matteo taught the volunteers scrap stock and worked Will’s prep station; they traded skills.
mem.zh: Matteo教志愿者用边角料熬汤，自己上了Will的切配台；两人互相学了手艺。
mem.ja: Matteo taught the volunteers scrap stock and worked Will’s prep station; they traded skills.
mem.ko: 나는 라들을 한 자원 봉사자 로사로 넘겨준다 그리고 그녀에게 비율을 보여준다. 그럼 나는 윌의 역할을 가져간다 그리고 따라잡으려고 시도한다.
mem.es: Matteo taught the volunteers scrap stock and worked Will’s prep station; they traded skills.

t.en: Leave the recipe; keep out of his way
t.zh: 留下做法，不去添乱
t.ja: 去る the recipe; keep out of his way
t.ko: 칼이 평평해. 팔꿈치 안에. 너는 양파가 너한테 돈을 빚진 것처럼 자르고 있어.
t.es: Leave the recipe; keep out of his way

en: I’ll write it down—ratios, times. I’d rather not be in your way at service.
I tape the card above the stockpot. It’s the neatest thing on that wall by a mile.
The soup makes the line. Matteo watches service from the doorway, learning the rhythm without touching it.
zh: 我写下来吧——配比、时间。出餐的时候我不想挡你的道。
我把卡片贴在汤锅上方。那是整面墙上最工整的东西，没有之一。
汤上了出餐线。Matteo站在门口看完了整场出餐，不上手，只记节奏。
ja: I’ll write it down—ratios, times. I’d rather not be in your way at service.
I tape the card above the stockpot. It’s the neatest thing on that wall by a mile.
The soup makes the line. Matteo watches service from the doorway, learning the rhythm without touching it.
ko: 11:30으로 수프가 라인에 있다, 그리고 마테오의 손들이 오랜 시간이 있는 양파처럼 냄새 난다.
마테오가 자원 봉사자들한테 부스러기 재고를 가르쳤고 윌의 준비 역할에서 일했다; 그들이 능력을 트레이드했어.
es: I’ll write it down—ratios, times. I’d rather not be in your way at service.
I tape the card above the stockpot. It’s the neatest thing on that wall by a mile.
The soup makes the line. Matteo watches service from the doorway, learning the rhythm without touching it.

mem.en: Matteo left a written stock recipe and watched Will’s service from the doorway.
mem.zh: Matteo留下了写好的高汤做法，在门口看完了Will的出餐。
mem.ja: Matteo left a written stock recipe and watched Will’s service from the doorway.
mem.ko: 나는 그걸 써내겠어—비율, 시간. 나는 오히려 너의 방식에서 벗어나 있지 않을 거야.
mem.es: Matteo left a written stock recipe and watched Will’s service from the doorway.

t.en: Tell him the scraps were the whole lesson
t.zh: 告诉他：边角料就是全部的道理
t.ja: Tell him the scraps were the whole lesson
t.ko: 나는 재고 냄비 위에 카드를 테이핑한다. 그건 그 벽에 있는 깔끔한 것이다 한 마일로.
t.es: Tell him the scraps were the whole lesson

en: You throw away flavor because you’re in a hurry. That’s the whole lesson.
And you’d have them eating at one-fifteen. That’s mine.
They’re both right, which makes it worse. The soup still goes out. Monday’s tasting still stands.
zh: 你因为赶时间，把味道都扔了。道理就这一条。
而你会让他们一点一刻才吃上饭。这是我的道理。
两个人都对，这就更难办了。汤照样上了。周一的试菜也照样算数。
ja: You throw away flavor because you’re in a hurry. That’s the whole lesson.
And you’d have them eating at one-fifteen. That’s mine.
They’re both right, which makes it worse. The soup still goes out. Monday’s tasting still stands.
ko: 수프가 라인을 만든다. 마테오가 문에서 서비스를 본다, 그것을 건드리지 않고 리듬을 배우고.
마테오가 쓰인 재고 조리법을 남겼고 문에서 윌의 서비스를 봤다.
es: You throw away flavor because you’re in a hurry. That’s the whole lesson.
And you’d have them eating at one-fifteen. That’s mine.
They’re both right, which makes it worse. The soup still goes out. Monday’s tasting still stands.

mem.en: Matteo lectured Will about waste; Will pushed back about timing. Monday’s tasting still stands.
mem.zh: Matteo数落Will浪费，Will回敬他太慢。周一的试菜依然算数。
mem.ja: Matteo lectured Will about waste; Will pushed back about timing. Monday’s tasting still stands.
mem.ko: 너는 부스러기를 던진다 빨리하기 때문에. 그건 전체 수업이야.
mem.es: Matteo lectured Will about waste; Will pushed back about timing. Monday’s tasting still stands.

t.en: Simple, Difficult to Forget
t.zh: 简单，却难忘
t.ja: Simple, Difficult to 忘れる
t.ko: 그리고 너는 1:15에서 그들을 먹게 했을 것이다. 그건 내 것이야.
t.es: Simple, Difficult to Forget

goal.en: Settle the supper menu: one dish together, or two
goal.zh: 定下晚餐菜单：合做一道，还是各做各的
goal.ja: Settle the supper menu: one dish together, or two
goal.ko: 그들이 둘 다 맞다, 그건 더 악화시킨다. 수프는 여전히 간다. 월요일의 시식이 여전히 있다.
goal.es: Settle the supper menu: one dish together, or two

place.ko: 마테오가 윌을 낭비에 대해 강의했다; 윌이 타이밍에 대해 다시 밀었다. 월요일의 시식이 여전히 있다.

en: Two plates on the steel pass. Will’s: braised chicken thighs, rice, greens. Matteo’s: the same chicken three ways, with a foam.
I eat his. It’s incredible. It’s also going to take four hundred minutes to plate.
I push the foam around with a spoon. Then I set the spoon down and don’t pick it back up.
I spent years making it complicated.
Then make simple difficult to forget.
If I serve rice and chicken, people will say anyone could have made it.
People will say it was the best rice and chicken they ever had. Different sentence.
My grandmother’s beans. I could make them asleep. I have never once put them on a menu.
zh: 不锈钢出菜台上并排两盘。Will的：红烧鸡腿、米饭、青菜。Matteo的：同一只鸡的三种做法，外加一层泡沫。
我吃了他的。好吃得不得了。也意味着装四百盘要花四百分钟。
我用勺子把泡沫推来推去，然后放下勺子，没再拿起来。
我花了好多年，把菜做复杂。
那就把简单做得让人忘不掉。
要是我端出鸡肉饭，大家会说，谁都做得出来。
大家会说，这是他们吃过最好的鸡肉饭。这是两句不一样的话。
外婆的豆子。我闭着眼都能做。可我从没把它写进任何一份菜单。
ja: Two plates on the steel pass. Will’s: braised chicken thighs, rice, greens. Matteo’s: the same chicken three ways, with a foam.
I eat his. It’s incredible. It’s also going to take four hundred minutes to plate.
I push the foam around with a spoon. Then I set the spoon down and don’t pick it back up.
I spent years making it complicated.
Then make simple difficult to forget.
If I serve rice and chicken, people will say anyone could have made it.
People will say it was the best rice and chicken they ever had. Different sentence.
My grandmother’s beans. I could make them asleep. I have never once put them on a menu.
ko: 저녁 메뉴를 정하자: 한 접시 함께, 또는 둘
강철 통로에 두 접시. 윌의: 조려진 닭다리, 쌀, 채소. 마테오의: 같은 닭고기 3가지 방식, 한 거품과.
나는 그의 것을 먹는다. 그건 불가능해. 그건 또한 400분을 플레이하는 데로 간다.
나는 강철 위에 여론을 미는데 그럼 내가 다시 집어올리지 않는다.
나는 년을 복잡하게 만드는 데 보냈다.

ask.en: What menu does Matteo put forward?
ask.ja: 何 menu does Matteo put forward?
ask.ko: 누군가가 그걸 간단함이라고 말하면, 그들은 누군가가 그걸 할 수 있었다고 말할 거야.
ask.es: What menu does Matteo put forward?

t.en: Build one dish together—both names on the card
t.zh: 合做一道菜——菜单卡上写两个人的名字
t.ja: Build one dish together—both names on the card
t.ko: 누군가가 그걸 최고의 쌀과 닭고기라고 말할 거야 그들이 절대 가졌다고. 다른 문장.
t.es: Build one dish together—both names on the card

en: One dish. My grandmother’s beans under your chicken. Both our names on it.
I write it on the whiteboard: FERRANTE / DORSEY. Then I underline it twice, which for me is a lot.
They taste it together at five. Neither says a word, which in a kitchen is the loudest review there is.
zh: 一道菜。外婆的豆子，垫在你的鸡肉底下。署我们两个人的名字。
我把它写上白板：FERRANTE / DORSEY。然后画了两道下划线——对我来说，这已经很隆重了。
五点钟，两人一起试吃。谁都没说话——在厨房里，这是最响亮的好评。
ja: One dish. My grandmother’s beans under your chicken. Both our names on it.
I write it on the whiteboard: FERRANTE / DORSEY. Then I underline it twice, which for me is a lot.
They taste it together at five. Neither says a word, which in a kitchen is the loudest review there is.
ko: 내 할머니의 콩들. 나는 그들을 자면서 만들 수 있어. 나는 절대 메뉴에 그들을 넣지 않았어.
함께 한 접시를 만들어—둘 다 이름이 카드에
es: One dish. My grandmother’s beans under your chicken. Both our names on it.
I write it on the whiteboard: FERRANTE / DORSEY. Then I underline it twice, which for me is a lot.
They taste it together at five. Neither says a word, which in a kitchen is the loudest review there is.

mem.en: Matteo and Will created one shared supper dish—beans under braised chicken—credited to both.
mem.zh: Matteo和Will合创了一道晚餐主菜——豆子配红烧鸡——署两人的名字。
mem.ja: Matteo and Will created one shared supper dish—beans under braised chicken—credited to both.
mem.ko: 한 접시. 내 할머니의 콩들이 너의 닭고기 아래. 둘 다 우리 이름.
mem.es: Matteo and Will created one shared supper dish—beans under braised chicken—credited to both.

t.en: Run two menus, but share every number
t.zh: 各出一份菜单，但所有数据共享
t.ja: Run two menus, but share every number
t.ko: 나는 화이트 보드에 그걸 적는다: 페란테 / 도르시. 그럼 내가 두 번을 밑줄 긋는데, 나를 위해 많이다.
t.es: Run two menus, but share every number

en: Two menus. Yours on the line, mine as a plated option. But I work from your counts—allergies, headcount, all of it.
Deal. You get the list. Not the say.
They split the whiteboard down the middle. The allergy list runs straight across both halves.
zh: 两份菜单。你的走出餐线，我的做单独装盘的选项。但我按你的数据来——过敏、人数，全部。
成交。名单给你，拍板权不给。
他们把白板从中间一分为二。过敏清单横跨两半，一路写到底。
ja: Two menus. Yours on the line, mine as a plated option. But I work from your counts—allergies, headcount, all of it.
Deal. You get the list. Not the say.
They split the whiteboard down the middle. The allergy list runs straight across both halves.
ko: 그들이 5시간에 맛본다 각각. 어느 것도 한 단어도 말하지 않는데, 부엌에서 그건 가장 시끄러운 리뷰다.
마테오와 윌이 한 공유 저녁 요리를 만들었다—콩들이 조려진 닭고기 아래—둘 다 신용을 받았어.
2개 메뉴들을 운영해, 하지만 매 숫자를 나누자
es: Two menus. Yours on the line, mine as a plated option. But I work from your counts—allergies, headcount, all of it.
Deal. You get the list. Not the say.
They split the whiteboard down the middle. The allergy list runs straight across both halves.

mem.en: They kept separate menus but agreed to share guest counts and dietary information.
mem.zh: 两人保留各自菜单，但约定共享人数与饮食禁忌信息。
mem.ja: They kept separate menus but agreed to share guest counts and dietary information.
mem.ko: 2개 메뉴들. 너의 라인에 있는 내 것, 한 플레이팅된 선택으로. 그런데 나는 너의 수에서 작동해—알레르기들, 손님수, 모두.
mem.es: They kept separate menus but agreed to share guest counts and dietary information.

t.en: Keep your menu and win the room
t.zh: 坚持自己的菜单，把全场赢过来
t.ja: 保つ your menu and win the room
t.ko: 좋아. 너는 목록을 얻어. 선택 아니라.
t.es: Keep your menu and win the room

en: Let the guests choose. Yours or mine. We’ll see what they come back for.
It’s not a cook-off, Matteo. The walk-in doesn’t know we’re competing.
Matteo orders extra short rib for his plate anyway. Nobody checks it against the delivery list. Yet.
zh: 让客人选。你的还是我的。看他们回头来要哪一份。
这不是厨艺比赛，Matteo。冷库可不知道我们在较劲。
Matteo还是给自己那道菜多订了牛小排。没人拿它去对送货单。暂时还没有。
ja: Let the guests choose. Yours or mine. We’ll see what they come back for.
It’s not a cook-off, Matteo. The walk-in doesn’t know we’re competing.
Matteo orders extra short rib for his plate anyway. Nobody checks it against the delivery list. Yet.
ko: 그들이 화이트 보드를 나눈다 아래로 반만. 알레르기 목록이 양쪽을 달린다.
그들이 분리 메뉴들을 유지했으나 손님 수와 식이 정보를 나누기로 동의했어.
es: Let the guests choose. Yours or mine. We’ll see what they come back for.
It’s not a cook-off, Matteo. The walk-in doesn’t know we’re competing.
Matteo orders extra short rib for his plate anyway. Nobody checks it against the delivery list. Yet.

mem.en: Matteo insisted on competing menus and ordered extra short rib without checking supply.
mem.zh: Matteo坚持两份菜单竞争，并在未核对供货的情况下多订了牛小排。
mem.ja: Matteo insisted on competing menus and ordered extra short rib without checking supply.
mem.ko: 손님들이 선택하게 해. 너의 또는 내 것. 우린 봤다 그들이 뭘 다시 와서 원하는지.
mem.es: Matteo insisted on competing menus and ordered extra short rib without checking supply.

t.en: Count Before You Promise
t.zh: 先数再说
t.ja: Count Before You Promise
t.ko: 그건 아니야 한 요리 경쟁, 마테오. 워크인이 우리가 경쟁하고 있다는 걸 모른다.
t.es: Count Before You Promise

goal.zh: 面对真实的缺口——不靠奇迹
goal.ko: 마테오가 대신 여분의 짧은 등갈비를 주문한다 아무도 배달 목록과 그것을 체크하지 않는 것 없이. 아직.

place.ko: 마테오가 경쟁 메뉴들을 고집하고 공급을 체크하지 않고 여분의 짧은 등갈비를 주문했어.

en: The Friday delivery comes in light: sixty pounds short on chicken, and half the greens the invoice swears to.
I take a marker to the whiteboard and cross out 400. My hand does not want to.
And offer what we can actually make.
The walk-in hums. Down the hall, a volunteer is cheerfully printing four hundred menus.
zh: 周五的货到了，分量不对：鸡肉少了六十磅，青菜只有发票上写的一半。
我拿起马克笔，在白板上划掉“400”。手不太愿意。
然后拿出我们真做得出来的东西。
冷库嗡嗡作响。走廊那头，一位志愿者正兴高采烈地打印四百份菜单。
ja: The 金曜日 delivery comes in light: sixty pounds short on chicken, and half the greens the invoice swears to.
I take a marker to the whiteboard and cross out 400. My hand does not want to.
And offer what we can actually make.
The walk-in hums. Down the hall, a volunteer is cheerfully printing four hundred menus.
ko: 금요일 배달이 가볍게 온다: 닭고기에서 60 파운드가 짧고, 그 발송 인보이스가 서약한 채소의 반.
나는 400을 지운다 화이트 보드에 마커로. 내 손이 하고 싶어 하지 않는다.
그리고 뭘 우리가 실제로 만들 수 있어 제공해.
es: The Friday delivery comes in light: sixty pounds short on chicken, and half the greens the invoice swears to.
I take a marker to the whiteboard and cross out 400. My hand does not want to.
And offer what we can actually make.
The walk-in hums. Down the hall, a volunteer is cheerfully printing four hundred menus.

ask.en: What does Matteo do about the shortfall?
ask.ja: 何 does Matteo do about the shortfall?
ask.es: What does Matteo do about the shortfall?

t.en: Call the partners now and say the real number
t.zh: 马上打给合作方，报真实数字
t.ja: Call the partners now and say the real number
t.ko: 그건 아니야.
t.es: Call the partners now and say the real number

en: I call the church pantry and the Tuesday market farmer myself. I say the number out loud. It’s smaller than I’d like.
That’s what honest sounds like. Not pretty. Useful.
By seven there’s a revised count, a notice for the doors, and thirty extra pounds of dried beans on the way.
zh: 我亲自打给教会食物站和周二集市的农户，把数字大声报出来。比我希望的要小。
诚实听起来就是这样。不好听，但有用。
到七点，新的份数定了，门口的告示写好了，另外三十磅干豆子也在路上了。
ja: I call the church pantry and the Tuesday market farmer myself. I say the number out loud. It’s smaller than I’d like.
That’s what honest sounds like. Not pretty. Useful.
By seven there’s a revised count, a notice for the doors, and thirty extra pounds of dried beans on the way.
ko: 워크인이 윙윙거린다. 복도 아래, 한 자원 봉사자가 밝게 400개 메뉴들을 인쇄하고 있다.
이제 파트너들을 부르고 진짜 숫자를 말해
es: I call the church pantry and the Tuesday market farmer myself. I say the number out loud. It’s smaller than I’d like.
That’s what honest sounds like. Not pretty. Useful.
By seven there’s a revised count, a notice for the doors, and thirty extra pounds of dried beans on the way.

mem.en: Matteo helped call partners with the true shortfall; they posted an honest revised count.
mem.zh: Matteo帮忙向合作方如实报了缺口，两人贴出了诚实的新份数。
mem.ja: Matteo helped call partners with the true shortfall; they posted an honest revised count.
mem.ko: 나는 교회 팬트리와 화요일 시장 농부를 나한테 부르는데 숫자를 말한다 크게. 그건 내가 좋아할 것보다 더 작다.
mem.es: Matteo helped call partners with the true shortfall; they posted an honest revised count.

t.en: Rework portions tonight; announce at nine
t.zh: 今晚重算份量，明早九点公布
t.ja: Rework portions tonight; announce at nine
t.ko: 그건 정직한 게 어떻게 소리나는지다. 이쁘지 않아. 유용해.
t.es: Rework portions tonight; announce at nine

en: Give me tonight. I’ll rework portions so everyone gets a real plate—then we announce at nine a.m. with real numbers.
Nine. Not ten. Not ‘after we see.’
Matteo recalculates until midnight. Will stays—not to watch him. Just to hand him things.
zh: 给我一晚上。我重算份量，让每个人都拿到像样的一盘——明早九点用真实数字公布。
九点。不是十点，也不是“看情况再说”。
Matteo一直算到半夜。Will也留下了——不是盯着他，只是给他递东西。
ja: Give me tonight. I’ll rework portions so everyone gets a real plate—then we announce at nine a.m. with real numbers.
Nine. Not ten. Not ‘after we see.’
Matteo recalculates until midnight. Will stays—not to watch him. Just to hand him things.
ko: 7시간에 의해 한 수정된 수, 문 설명, 그리고 30 여분 파운드의 말린 콩들이 길에 있어.
마테오가 파트너들한테 진짜 부족으로 부르는 것을 도왔고; 그들이 진짜 수정된 수를 게시했어.
오늘 밤 일부를 다시 작업해; 9시에 알려
es: Give me tonight. I’ll rework portions so everyone gets a real plate—then we announce at nine a.m. with real numbers.
Nine. Not ten. Not ‘after we see.’
Matteo recalculates until midnight. Will stays—not to watch him. Just to hand him things.

mem.en: Matteo reworked portions overnight; they agreed to announce the real count at 9 a.m.
mem.zh: Matteo连夜重算份量，两人约定早上九点公布真实份数。
mem.ja: Matteo reworked portions overnight; they agreed to announce the real count at 9 a.m.
mem.ko: 나한테 오늘 밤을 줘. 나는 일부를 다시 작동시킬 거야 그래서 모든 사람이 한 진짜 접시를 얻는다—그럼 우린 실제 숫자와 9시간에 알려.
mem.es: Matteo reworked portions overnight; they agreed to announce the real count at 9 a.m.

t.en: Handle the food; leave the promise to Will
t.zh: 只管做菜，承诺的事交给Will
t.ja: Handle the food; leave the promise to Will
t.ko: 9시간. 10이 아니야. '우리가 봤다 후에' 아니라.
t.es: Handle the food; leave the promise to Will

en: The count is your conversation. I’ll cook whatever number it turns out to be.
I nod. I make the calls alone. It’s fine. I’m good at alone.
The notice goes up late. The food will be fine. The partnership is thinner.
zh: 份数是你要去谈的事。最后是多少，我就做多少。
我点点头，一个人把电话打完了。没关系。一个人我很拿手。
告示贴得晚了些。饭菜不会有问题。搭档之间，却薄了一层。
ja: The count is your conversation. I’ll cook whatever number it turns out to be.
I nod. I make the calls alone. It’s fine. I’m good at alone.
The notice goes up late. The food will be fine. The partnership is thinner.
ko: 마테오가 자정까지 일부를 다시 작동시킨다. 윌이 있다—그를 보기 위해서가 아니라. 그냥 그한테 물건을 건네주려고.
마테오가 밤새 일부를 다시 작동시켰다; 그들이 9시간에 진짜 수를 알리기로 동의했어.
es: The count is your conversation. I’ll cook whatever number it turns out to be.
I nod. I make the calls alone. It’s fine. I’m good at alone.
The notice goes up late. The food will be fine. The partnership is thinner.

mem.en: Matteo left the public count to Will, who made the partner calls alone.
mem.zh: Matteo把对外公布份数的事留给Will，Will独自打完了所有电话。
mem.ja: Matteo left the public count to Will, who made the partner calls alone.
mem.ko: 수는 너의 대화다. 나는 어떤 숫자로든 요리할 거야 그게 되어 나온다.
mem.es: Matteo left the public count to Will, who made the partner calls alone.

t.en: The Last Hour
t.zh: 最后一小时
t.ja: The Last 時間
t.ko: 나는 고개를 끄덕인다. 나는 파트너들한테 혼자 전화한다. 그건 좋다. 나는 혼자가 좋다.
t.es: The Last Hour

goal.en: Portion by what’s really in the pans
goal.zh: 按锅里真实有的来分份
goal.ja: Portion by what’s really in the pans
goal.ko: 설명이 늦게 간다. 음식이 좋을 거야. 파트너십이 더 얇다.
goal.es: Portion by what’s really in the pans

place.zh: 东区公共活动厅，出餐窗口
place.ko: 마테오가 공개 수를 윌에게 남겼다, 혼자 파트너 호출을 했어.

en: One hour to doors. The line already bends past the bus shelter. Inside: four hotel pans, two soup pots, and a clipboard that refuses to lie.
How many can we feed well?
I count pans, then ladles, then ladles per pan. Twice. The way I’d check a tasting menu.
I count the line from the window. I stop when the number gets bigger than the pans.
Three hundred forty full plates. Or four hundred smaller ones nobody remembers.
Or three-forty full, and sixty bowls of your soup with bread. That’s not a lesser plate. It’s a different one.
He isn’t asking me to make it stretch. He’s asking me to make it true.
zh: 离开门还有一小时。队伍已经拐过了公交站。屋里：四只大餐盘，两锅汤，还有一块拒绝说谎的夹板。
我们能好好喂饱多少人？
我数餐盘，再数汤勺，再数每盘能舀几勺。数了两遍。就像核对品鉴菜单那样。
我从窗口数队伍。数到比餐盘还多的时候，我停了。
三百四十份满盘。或者四百份没人记得住的小份。
或者三百四十份满盘，再加六十碗你的汤配面包。那不是次一等的饭，是另一种饭。
他没让我把饭变多。他是让我把话说真。
ja: One hour to doors. The line already bends past the bus shelter. Inside: four hotel pans, two soup pots, and a clipboard that refuses to lie.
どのように many can we feed well?
I count pans, then ladles, then ladles per pan. Twice. The way I’d check a tasting menu.
I count the line from the window. I stop when the number gets bigger than the pans.
Three hundred forty full plates. Or four hundred smaller ones nobody remembers.
Or three-forty full, and sixty bowls of your soup with bread. That’s not a lesser plate. It’s a different one.
He isn’t asking me to make it stretch. He’s asking me to make it true.
ko: 일부로 몇 명이 정말 팬에 있는지에 따라
한 시간이 문들에 있다. 라인이 이미 버스 쉼터 과거로 구부린다. 안에: 4개 호텔 팬들, 2개 수프 냄비들, 그리고 한 클립 보드 거짓말을 거절한다.
우리가 얼마나 많이 잘 먹일 수 있어?
나는 팬들을 센다, 그럼 라들, 그럼 라들당 라들. 두 번. 내가 어떻게 음식 선택 메뉴를 체크할 것처럼.
나는 창에서 라인을 센다. 나는 멈춘다 수가 팬들보다 더 커질 때.
es: One hour to doors. The line already bends past the bus shelter. Inside: four hotel pans, two soup pots, and a clipboard that refuses to lie.
How many can we feed well?
I count pans, then ladles, then ladles per pan. Twice. The way I’d check a tasting menu.
I count the line from the window. I stop when the number gets bigger than the pans.
Three hundred forty full plates. Or four hundred smaller ones nobody remembers.
Or three-forty full, and sixty bowls of your soup with bread. That’s not a lesser plate. It’s a different one.
He isn’t asking me to make it stretch. He’s asking me to make it true.

ask.en: How does Matteo plate the last hour?
ask.ja: どのように does Matteo plate the last hour?
ask.ko: 3백 40 가득한 접시들. 또는 400 더 작은 것들 아무도 기억하지 않는.
ask.es: How does Matteo plate the last hour?

t.en: Three-forty full plates, sixty soup-and-bread
t.zh: 三百四十份满盘，六十碗汤配面包
t.ja: Three-forty full plates, sixty soup-and-bread
t.ko: 또는 3 백 40 가득함, 그리고 60 수프로 된 그릇들과 빵으로. 그건 한 더 작은 접시가 아니야. 그건 다른 것이야.
t.es: Three-forty full plates, sixty soup-and-bread

en: I tell the door volunteers the real plan: the last sixty get soup and bread, and bread seconds for anyone who wants them.
I plate the soup bowls like they’re going to my counter. Same care. No foam.
Nobody reaches an empty pan. Nobody is told a story they’ll later find out wasn’t true.
zh: 我把真实安排告诉门口的志愿者：最后六十位是汤配面包，面包谁想添都可以。
我盛那些汤碗，就像要端上我自己的吧台。一样用心。不加泡沫。
没人排到空锅前。也没人听到一个事后才发现不是真的故事。
ja: I tell the door volunteers the real plan: the last sixty get soup and bread, and bread seconds for anyone who wants them.
I plate the soup bowls like they’re going to my counter. Same care. No foam.
Nobody reaches an empty pan. Nobody is told a story they’ll later find out wasn’t true.
ko: 그는 나한테 나를 그 다시 만들려고 하는 걸 요청하고 있지 않다. 그는 나한테 그걸 참으로 만들도록 요청하고 있다.
es: I tell the door volunteers the real plan: the last sixty get soup and bread, and bread seconds for anyone who wants them.
I plate the soup bowls like they’re going to my counter. Same care. No foam.
Nobody reaches an empty pan. Nobody is told a story they’ll later find out wasn’t true.

mem.en: They served 340 full plates and 60 bowls of soup with bread, announced honestly at the door.
mem.zh: 两人供应了340份满盘与60碗汤配面包，并在门口如实告知。
mem.ja: They served 340 full plates and 60 bowls of soup with bread, announced honestly at the door.
mem.ko: 나는 문 자원 봉사자들한테 진짜 계획을 말한다: 마지막 60은 수프와 빵을 얻는다, 그리고 빵 두 번과를 아무도 원하는 사람.
mem.es: They served 340 full plates and 60 bowls of soup with bread, announced honestly at the door.

t.en: Equal smaller plates, plus pantry to-go bags
t.zh: 人人同样的小份，再加食物站的外带袋
t.ja: Equal smaller plates, plus pantry to-go bags
t.ko: 나는 수프 그릇들을 마치 그들이 내 카운터로 갈 것처럼 플레이팅한다. 같은 배려. 거품 없어.
t.es: Equal smaller plates, plus pantry to-go bags

en: Everyone gets the same plate, smaller, plus the pantry’s to-go bags for tomorrow. Same meal for all four hundred.
Fair. Tell them it’s smaller before they sit, not after.
The plates are smaller. The to-go bags are heavy. The line notices both, and nobody feels tricked.
zh: 每人一样的一盘，份量小一点，再加上食物站明天吃的外带袋。四百个人吃同一顿饭。
公平。但要在他们坐下前说份量小，而不是之后。
盘子小了，外带袋沉甸甸的。队伍里的人两样都注意到了，没人觉得被糊弄。
ja: Everyone gets the same plate, smaller, plus the pantry’s to-go bags for tomorrow. Same meal for all four hundred.
Fair. Tell them it’s smaller before they sit, not after.
The plates are smaller. The to-go bags are heavy. The line notices both, and nobody feels tricked.
ko: 아무도가 한 비어있는 팬에 도달하지 않는다. 아무도가 이제 나중에 그들이 알아낼 거 아닌 이야기를 말해진다.
그들이 340 가득한 접시들과 60 수프 그릇들과 빵을 제공했다, 정직하게 문에 알렸어.
같은 더 작은 접시들, 더하기 팬트리 가져가기-가방들
es: Everyone gets the same plate, smaller, plus the pantry’s to-go bags for tomorrow. Same meal for all four hundred.
Fair. Tell them it’s smaller before they sit, not after.
The plates are smaller. The to-go bags are heavy. The line notices both, and nobody feels tricked.

mem.en: They served smaller equal plates to all 400, paired with pantry to-go bags, announced before seating.
mem.zh: 两人给四百人都提供了同样的小份，配上食物站外带袋，并在入座前说明。
mem.ja: They served smaller equal plates to all 400, paired with pantry to-go bags, announced before seating.
mem.ko: 모든 사람이 같은 접시를 얻는다, 더 작은, 더하기 팬트리의 가져가기-가방들 내일. 같은 식사 모두 400명을 위해.
mem.es: They served smaller equal plates to all 400, paired with pantry to-go bags, announced before seating.

t.en: Keep your plates full-size; Will runs the line
t.zh: 你的盘子保持原份量，队伍交给Will
t.ja: 保つ your plates full-size; Will runs the line
t.ko: 공정해. 그들한테 그 더 작다고 말해 기 전에 앉기 전에, 과 후가 아니라.
t.es: Keep your plates full-size; Will runs the line

en: My plate stays the size it is. You manage what’s left.
I take the clipboard and move the last forty to pantry sandwiches. I say it out loud at the door. Nobody’s lied to.
It works. It isn’t what either of them wanted. Matteo’s plates are perfect, and he feels it anyway.
zh: 我的盘子份量不变。剩下的你来安排。
我拿过夹板，把最后四十位改成食物站的三明治，在门口大声说明。没有人被骗。
办成了。只是两人都不想这样。Matteo的每一盘都完美无缺，他心里却还是咯噔了一下。
ja: My plate stays the size it is. You manage what’s left.
I take the clipboard and move the last forty to pantry sandwiches. I say it out loud at the door. Nobody’s lied to.
It works. It isn’t what either of them wanted. Matteo’s plates are perfect, and he feels it anyway.
ko: 접시들이 더 작다. 가져가기-가방들이 무겁다. 라인이 둘 다 알아챈다, 그리고 아무도 속은 거 같지 않다.
그들이 같은 더 작은 접시들을 400명을 제공했다, 팬트리 가져가기-가방들과 짝을 지었다, 기 전에 기하학을 알렸어.
너의 접시를 가득하게 유지해; 윌이 라인을 운영해
es: My plate stays the size it is. You manage what’s left.
I take the clipboard and move the last forty to pantry sandwiches. I say it out loud at the door. Nobody’s lied to.
It works. It isn’t what either of them wanted. Matteo’s plates are perfect, and he feels it anyway.

mem.en: Matteo kept his full plates; Will moved the last forty guests to pantry sandwiches with an honest notice.
mem.zh: Matteo保持了满盘份量；Will把最后四十位客人改为食物站三明治，并如实告知。
mem.ja: Matteo kept his full plates; Will moved the last forty guests to pantry sandwiches with an honest notice.
mem.ko: 내 접시가 그게 있는 크기를 유지한다. 너는 남은 것을 관리한다.
mem.es: Matteo kept his full plates; Will moved the last forty guests to pantry sandwiches with an honest notice.

t.en: The Plate He Saved
t.zh: 他留下的那一盘
t.ja: The Plate He Saved
t.ko: 나는 클립 보드를 가지고 간다 그리고 마지막 40을 팬트리 샌드위치들로 옮긴다. 나는 그걸 문에서 크게 말한다. 아무도가 거짓말을 한 게 아니다.
t.es: The Plate He Saved

goal.en: Find out who the last plate is for
goal.zh: 弄清最后一盘是留给谁的
goal.ja: 見つける out who the last plate is for
goal.ko: 그건 작동한다. 그건 그들이 원한 뭐도 아니다. 마테오의 접시들이 완벽하고, 그리고 그가 여전히 그걸 느낀다.
goal.es: Find out who the last plate is for

place.ko: 마테오가 가득한 접시들을 유지했다; 윌이 마지막 40을 팬트리 샌드위치들로 옮겼다 진짜 설명과.

en: Chairs up, floors wet, the dish machine on its last cycle. On the pass, under a clean towel, sits one full plate.
I lift the towel. Chicken, beans, greens, the good crust from the pan edge. Plated carefully—by someone who doesn’t plate carefully.
I’m drying hotel pans that are already dry.
You didn’t eat. I watched you not eat for six hours.
You didn’t save one for yourself.
I was hoping you’d ask me to share.
One plate. Two people who just fed four hundred. For once, the math is easy.
zh: 椅子倒扣上桌，地面湿漉漉的，洗碗机在跑最后一轮。出菜台上，一块干净毛巾底下，盖着满满一盘。
我掀开毛巾。鸡肉、豆子、青菜，还有锅边最香的那层焦皮。摆得很仔细——出自一个平时从不仔细摆盘的人。
我在擦几只早就干了的餐盘。
你一口没吃。我看着你六个小时一口没吃。
我本来希望你会叫我一起吃。
一盘饭，两个刚喂饱了四百人的人。这道算术，总算简单了一回。
ja: Chairs up, floors wet, the dish machine on its last cycle. On the pass, under a clean towel, sits one full plate.
I lift the towel. Chicken, beans, greens, the good crust from the pan edge. Plated carefully—by someone who doesn’t plate carefully.
I’m drying hotel pans that are already dry.
You didn’t eat. I watched you not eat for six hours.
You didn’t save one for yourself.
I was hoping you’d ask me to share.
One plate. Two people who just fed four hundred. For once, the math is easy.
ko: 의자들 올라, 바닥들 젖어, 통로에, 한 깨끗한 수건 아래, 한 가득한 접시가 앉는다.
나는 수건을 든다. 닭고기, 콩들, 채소들, 팬 가장자리에서 좋은 껍질. 조심스럽게 플레이팅된—누군가 조심스럽게 플레이팅하지 않는 사람에 의해.
나는 이미 말린 호텔 팬들을 말리고 있다.
너 6시간 먹지 않은 걸 보지 않았어.
es: Chairs up, floors wet, the dish machine on its last cycle. On the pass, under a clean towel, sits one full plate.
I lift the towel. Chicken, beans, greens, the good crust from the pan edge. Plated carefully—by someone who doesn’t plate carefully.
I’m drying hotel pans that are already dry.
You didn’t eat. I watched you not eat for six hours.
You didn’t save one for yourself.
I was hoping you’d ask me to share.
One plate. Two people who just fed four hundred. For once, the math is easy.

ask.en: What does Matteo do with the last plate?
ask.ja: 何 does Matteo do with the last plate?
ask.ko: 너 너를 위해 하나를 구하지 않았다.
ask.es: What does Matteo do with the last plate?

t.en: Hand him the second fork
t.zh: 递给他第二把叉子
t.ja: 手 him the second fork
t.ko: 나 너가 나한테 나누기를 물어주길 바랐어.
t.es: Hand him the second fork

en: I take a second fork from the bin and hold it out handle-first, the way you pass a knife.
zh: 我从筐里拿出第二把叉子，柄朝他递过去，就像递刀那样。
ja: I take a second fork from the bin and hold it out handle-first, the way you pass a knife.
ko: 한 접시. 두 사람이 방금 400을 먹였다. 한 번, 수학이 쉽다.
es: I take a second fork from the bin and hold it out handle-first, the way you pass a knife.

mem.en: Matteo handed Will the second fork and they shared the last plate.
mem.zh: Matteo把第二把叉子递给Will，两人分吃了最后一盘。
mem.ja: Matteo handed Will the second fork and they shared the last plate.
mem.ko: 나는 빈에서 두 번째 포크를 가져다 넘겨주고 그걸 손잡이-처음으로 들고, 포크를 어떻게 지나갈지 같이.
mem.es: Matteo handed Will the second fork and they shared the last plate.

t.en: Split it onto two plates and sit across
t.zh: 分成两盘，面对面坐下
t.ja: Split it onto two plates and sit across
t.ko: 너 무언가 말해야 했어.
t.es: Split it onto two plates and sit across

en: I get a second plate and divide it exactly, because I am who I am.
I’d like us both to have enough first. Then we’ll see.
zh: 我拿来第二只盘子，分得分毫不差——我就是这样的人。
我想先让我们俩都吃够。然后再说。
ja: I get a second plate and divide it exactly, because I am who I am.
I’d like us both to have enough first. Then we’ll see.
ko: 마테오가 윌한테 두 번째 포크를 넘겨줬고 마지막 접시를 나눴어.
그걸 두 개 접시에 나누고 건너편 앉아
es: I get a second plate and divide it exactly, because I am who I am.
I’d like us both to have enough first. Then we’ll see.

mem.en: Matteo divided the last plate evenly onto two and they ate across from each other.
mem.zh: Matteo把最后一盘平分成两盘，两人面对面吃完。
mem.ja: Matteo divided the last plate evenly onto two and they ate across from each other.
mem.ko: 나는 두 번째 접시를 얻고 나는 그건 나야 왜냐하면 나는 누구인지 정확히 나눈다.
mem.es: Matteo divided the last plate evenly onto two and they ate across from each other.

t.en: Wrap it for him and go home
t.zh: 给他包好，自己回家
t.ja: Wrap it for him and go home
t.ko: 너 그걸 재었어.
t.es: Wrap it for him and go home

en: I wrap it in foil, write WILL on the lid in marker, and set it in his hands.
You should eat this. I need to go home tonight—alone. It isn’t about the plate.
Okay. Thanks for saying it straight.
zh: 我用锡纸包好，拿马克笔在盖子上写了WILL，放到他手里。
这个你该吃。我今晚得回家——一个人。跟这盘饭无关。
ja: I wrap it in foil, write WILL on the lid in marker, and set it in his hands.
You should eat this. I need to go home tonight—alone. It isn’t about the plate.
Okay. Thanks for saying it straight.
ko: 나는 먼저 우린 둘 다 가졌다면 충분하길 원할 거야. 그럼 우린 봤다.
마테오가 두 개 접시들로 마지막을 나누고 그들이 건너편에 앉아 먹었어.
es: I wrap it in foil, write WILL on the lid in marker, and set it in his hands.
You should eat this. I need to go home tonight—alone. It isn’t about the plate.
Okay. Thanks for saying it straight.

mem.en: Matteo wrapped the plate for Will and went home alone; Will thanked him for being direct.
mem.zh: Matteo把饭包好留给Will，独自回了家；Will谢谢他说得直接。
mem.ja: Matteo wrapped the plate for Will and went home alone; Will thanked him for being direct.
mem.ko: 나는 그걸 호일에 감싸고, 그 뚜껑에 WILL을 표로 적고, 그리고 그의 손에 그걸 설정한다.
mem.es: Matteo wrapped the plate for Will and went home alone; Will thanked him for being direct.

t.en: The Second Fork
t.zh: 第二把叉
t.ja: The 秒 Fork
t.ko: 너 이걸 먹어야 해. 나는 오늘 밤 집에 가야 해—혼자. 그건 접시에 대해 아니야.
t.es: The Second Fork

goal.en: Ask for a dinner neither of them has to serve
goal.zh: 约一顿谁都不用上菜的晚饭
goal.ja: Ask for a dinner neither of them has to serve
goal.es: Ask for a dinner neither of them has to serve

place.en: Eastside Commons Kitchen, after lunch service
place.zh: 东区公共厨房，午餐出完后
place.ja: Eastside Commons Kitchen, after lunch service
place.ko: 마테오가 그걸 윌을 위해 감싸고 혼자 집에 갔어; 윌이 그에게 직접 감사했어.
place.es: Eastside Commons Kitchen, after lunch service

en: Three days later. Lunch is done. Will sets a full plate on the steel table out of habit. Matteo walks in carrying two forks from his own restaurant.
You brought your own silverware to a community kitchen.
This one is not for a review.
I set the forks down parallel. Then, deliberately, I nudge one crooked.
When neither of us is serving.
We’ll count the hours before we promise.
zh: 三天后。午餐出完了。Will习惯性地把满满一盘放上不锈钢桌。Matteo走进来，手里拿着两把他自己餐厅的叉子。
你带自己的餐具来社区厨房？
这一盘，不是给人评分的。
我把两把叉子并排放好。然后，故意把其中一把拨歪。
在我们俩谁都不用上菜的时候。
我们先把时间数清楚，再许诺。
ja: Three days later. Lunch is done. Will sets a full plate on the steel table out of habit. Matteo walks in carrying two forks from his own restaurant.
You brought your own silverware to a community kitchen.
This one is not for a review.
I set the forks down parallel. Then, deliberately, I nudge one crooked.
いつ neither of us is serving.
We’ll count the hours before we promise.
ko: 어느 누구도 서빙할 필요 없는 한 저녁을 요청해
이스트사이드 커뮌 부엌, 점심 서비스 후
3일 후. 점심이 끝났다. 윌이 습관에서 강철 테이블 위에 한 가득한 접시를 설정한다. 마테오가 자신의 음식점에서 두 포크를 들고 걸어온다.
너 한 공동체 부엌에 손가락 수가락을 가져왔어.
이 하나는 한 리뷰를 위해서가 아니다.
나는 포크들을 아래로 설정한다 평행로. 그럼, 의도적으로, 나는 하나를 구부린다.
es: Three days later. Lunch is done. Will sets a full plate on the steel table out of habit. Matteo walks in carrying two forks from his own restaurant.
You brought your own silverware to a community kitchen.
This one is not for a review.
I set the forks down parallel. Then, deliberately, I nudge one crooked.
When neither of us is serving.
We’ll count the hours before we promise.

ask.en: What does Matteo do with Friday?
ask.ja: What does Matteo do with 金曜日?
ask.ko: 한번도 우리가 서빙하는 건 아닐 때.
ask.es: What does Matteo do with Friday?

t.en: Count the hours together—then say yes
t.zh: 一起把时间数清楚——然后答应
t.ja: Count the hours together—then say yes
t.ko: 금요일?
t.es: Count the hours together—then say yes

en: I take out my phone. Friday: prep till four, a sous chef who owes me, service covered. I show him the screen.
Seven o’clock. My place. I’m cooking. You’re not allowed in the kitchen.
That will be very difficult for me. Yes.
zh: 我掏出手机。周五：备料到四点，一个欠我人情的副厨，晚市有人顶。我把屏幕给他看。
七点。我家。我做饭。你不准进厨房。
这对我来说会非常艰难。好。
ja: I take out my phone. 金曜日: prep till four, a sous chef who owes me, service covered. I show him the screen.
Seven o’clock. My place. I’m cooking. You’re not allowed in the kitchen.
That will be very difficult for me. Yes.
es: I take out my phone. Friday: prep till four, a sous chef who owes me, service covered. I show him the screen.
Seven o’clock. My place. I’m cooking. You’re not allowed in the kitchen.
That will be very difficult for me. Yes.

mem.en: Matteo and Will confirmed Friday dinner at 7 at Will’s place, with Will cooking.
mem.zh: Matteo和Will确定了周五七点在Will家吃晚饭，由Will下厨。
mem.ja: Matteo and Will confirmed Friday dinner at 7 at Will’s place, with Will cooking.
mem.ko: 나는 내 휴대폰을 꺼낸다. 금요일: 4시까지 준비, 한 수 셰프가 나한테 빚진다, 서비스 덮혔다. 나는 화면을 그한테 보여준다.
mem.es: Matteo and Will confirmed Friday dinner at 7 at Will’s place, with Will cooking.

t.en: Ask for Sunday lunch—as friends, for now
t.zh: 改约周日午饭——先做朋友
t.ja: Ask for Sunday lunch—as friends, for now
t.ko: 7시간. 내 장소. 나는 요리할 거야. 너는 부엌에 허용되지 않아.
t.es: Ask for Sunday lunch—as friends, for now

en: Not Friday. I’d like to be friends first, properly. Sunday lunch. Something plain.
Plain I can do. Friends I’m already doing. If the rest comes, I’ll be here.
They shake on it, which is ridiculous, and both of them know it.
zh: 不是周五。我想先好好做朋友。周日午饭，吃点简单的。
简单我会。朋友我已经在当了。其他的要是来了，我就在这儿。
两人握手成交，这很荒唐，他们俩心里都清楚。
ja: Not Friday. I’d like to be friends first, properly. Sunday lunch. Something plain.
Plain I can do. Friends I’m already doing. If the rest comes, I’ll be here.
They shake on it, which is ridiculous, and both of them know it.
ko: 그건 내게 극도로 어려울 거야. 그래.
마테오와 윌이 금요일 저녁을 7시에 확인했다 윌의 장소에서, 윌이 요리하고.
es: Not Friday. I’d like to be friends first, properly. Sunday lunch. Something plain.
Plain I can do. Friends I’m already doing. If the rest comes, I’ll be here.
They shake on it, which is ridiculous, and both of them know it.

mem.en: Matteo asked to be friends first; they set a plain Sunday lunch.
mem.zh: Matteo提出先做朋友，两人约了一顿简单的周日午饭。
mem.ja: Matteo asked to be friends first; they set a plain 日曜日 lunch.
mem.ko: 금요일 아니야. 난 먼저 친구들로 있고 싶어, 적절하게. 일요일 점심. 뭔가 일반.
mem.es: Matteo asked to be friends first; they set a plain Sunday lunch.

t.en: Say no—kindly, and mean it
t.zh: 拒绝——温和，但认真
t.ja: Say no—kindly, and mean it
t.ko: 일반 난 할 수 있어. 친구들 난 이미 하고 있어. 만약 나머지가 와, 난 여기 있을 거야.
t.es: Say no—kindly, and mean it

en: I don’t think I should. Not because of you. I don’t have a life that fits a dinner right now.
Okay. Thank you for counting before you promised.
Will pushes the plate across anyway. Food isn’t a proposal. It’s just lunch.
zh: 我想我不该答应。不是因为你。我现在的生活，塞不进一顿晚饭。
好。谢谢你先数清楚了，才没乱许诺。
Will还是把那盘饭推了过去。吃饭不是表白，只是午饭。
ja: I don’t think I should. Not because of you. I don’t have a life that fits a dinner right now.
Okay. Thank you for counting before you promised.
Will pushes the plate across anyway. Food isn’t a proposal. It’s just lunch.
ko: 마테오가 먼저 친구들로 있기를 요청했다; 그들이 일반 일요일 점심을 설정했어.
나는 생각해 안 된다고. 너 때문이 아니라. 나는 이제 한 삶이 가지지 않았다 한 저녁에 맞을 것.
es: I don’t think I should. Not because of you. I don’t have a life that fits a dinner right now.
Okay. Thank you for counting before you promised.
Will pushes the plate across anyway. Food isn’t a proposal. It’s just lunch.

mem.en: Matteo declined a private dinner; Will accepted it and still fed him lunch.
mem.zh: Matteo婉拒了私下的晚饭；Will接受了，仍然请他吃了午饭。
mem.ja: Matteo declined a private dinner; Will accepted it and still fed him lunch.
mem.ko: 좋아. 고마워 세기 전에 약속한 거 위해.
mem.es: Matteo declined a private dinner; Will accepted it and still fed him lunch.

t.en: Neither of Us Serving
t.zh: 谁都不必上菜
t.ja: Neither of Us Serving
t.ko: 윌이 어쨌든 접시를 밀어낸다. 음식이 한 제안이 아니다. 그건 그냥 점심이다.
t.es: Neither of Us Serving

goal.en: Decide what you are to each other, off the clock
goal.zh: 下了班，决定你们是什么关系
goal.ja: Decide what you are to each other, off the clock
goal.ko: 마테오가 한 사적인 저녁을 거절했다; 윌이 받아들였고 여전히 그한테 점심을 먹였다.
goal.es: Decide what you are to each other, off the clock

place.zh: 东区公共活动厅，活动复盘

time.ko: 오프 시간에 너가 서로 뭔지 결정해

en: The debrief. The coordinator reads the numbers: four hundred fed, no empty pans, one volunteer who cried over the soup, in a good way.
I sit on the counter because the chairs are stacked. I’ve been counting the hours since Tuesday.
The board wants the supper again next year, same two chefs. And Matteo’s restaurant manager has texted: ‘Heard about the beans. Can we talk?’
The beans were my grandmother’s. I’ve never cooked them for anyone who paid.
Then maybe you should. Full price. Not pity pricing—real food, real cost, real credit.
I keep feeding the eleven-thirty line. That part isn’t up for discussion. The rest is.
The rest is. He’s leaving the door open, and he isn’t holding it for me. I have to walk through on my own.
zh: 活动复盘。协调员念着数字：四百人吃上了饭，没有一只锅见底，一位志愿者对着汤哭了——是好的那种哭。
椅子都摞起来了，我就坐在台面上。从周二起，我一直在数时间。
理事会希望明年再办一次，还是这两位主厨。Matteo餐厅的经理也发来消息：“听说了豆子的事。聊聊？”
那豆子是我外婆的做法。我从没做给付钱的客人吃过。
那也许你该做了。全价。不是同情价——真材实料，真实成本，真名实姓。
我继续喂十一点半的队伍。这一条没得商量。其他的都可以谈。
其他的都可以谈。他把门留着，却没替我扶着。得我自己走过去。
ja: The debrief. The coordinator reads the numbers: four hundred fed, no empty pans, one volunteer who cried over the soup, in a good way.
I sit on the counter because the chairs are stacked. I’ve been counting the hours since Tuesday.
The board wants the supper again next year, same two chefs. And Matteo’s restaurant manager has texted: ‘Heard about the beans. Can we talk?’
The beans were my grandmother’s. I’ve never cooked them for anyone who paid.
Then maybe you should. Full price. Not pity pricing—real food, real cost, real credit.
I keep feeding the eleven-thirty line. That part isn’t up for discussion. The rest is.
The rest is. He’s leaving the door open, and he isn’t holding it for me. I have to walk through on my own.
ko: 토론. 코디네이터가 숫자들을 읽는다: 400 먹였다, 한 비어있는 팬 없음, 한 자원 봉사자가 울었다 수프에 대해, 좋은 방식으로.
나는 카운터 위에 앉아 의자들이 쌓여있다. 나는 화요일부터 시간들을 세고 있다.
보드가 원한다 다음 해에 저녁 다시, 같은 두 요리사들. 그리고 마테오의 음식점 매니저가 문자를 했다: '콩들에 대해 들었어. 우린 말할 수 있어?'
콩들은 내 할머니의 거였다. 나는 절대 그들을 누군가를 위해 요리했다 지불했던.
그럼 아마도 너 해야 해. 정가가. 그런게 가격—실제 음식, 실제 비용, 실제 신용.
es: The debrief. The coordinator reads the numbers: four hundred fed, no empty pans, one volunteer who cried over the soup, in a good way.
I sit on the counter because the chairs are stacked. I’ve been counting the hours since Tuesday.
The board wants the supper again next year, same two chefs. And Matteo’s restaurant manager has texted: ‘Heard about the beans. Can we talk?’
The beans were my grandmother’s. I’ve never cooked them for anyone who paid.
Then maybe you should. Full price. Not pity pricing—real food, real cost, real credit.
I keep feeding the eleven-thirty line. That part isn’t up for discussion. The rest is.
The rest is. He’s leaving the door open, and he isn’t holding it for me. I have to walk through on my own.

ask.en: What does Matteo choose, off the clock?
ask.ja: 何 does Matteo choose, off the clock?
ask.ko: 나는 11:30 라인을 먹이는 걸 계속한다. 그 부분이 논의에 올라오지 않아. 나머지는.
ask.es: What does Matteo choose, off the clock?

t.en: Dinner tonight—and a menu with both names
t.zh: 今晚一起吃饭——再写一份有两人名字的菜单
t.ja: Dinner tonight—and a menu with both names
t.ko: 나머지가 열려 있다. 그가 문을 열고 있다, 그리고 그가 나를 위해 그것을 들고 있지 않다. 나는 그를 통해 걸어가야 해 내 자신에서.
t.es: Dinner tonight—and a menu with both names

en: I hand him a card from my pocket. Handwritten: a six-seat supper, two chefs, full price, both names.
I wrote us a Friday. The menu is just where I keep things I mean.
Later, at Will’s table, nobody serves anybody. They pass the pan back and forth like they’ve done it for years.
zh: 我从兜里掏出一张卡片递给他。手写的：六人晚餐，两位主厨，全价，署两个名字。
我给我们写了一个周五。菜单只是我存放真心话的地方。
后来，在Will的饭桌上，谁也不用给谁上菜。那口锅在两人之间传来传去，像已经这样传了好多年。
ja: I hand him a card from my pocket. Handwritten: a six-seat supper, two chefs, full price, both names.
I wrote us a 金曜日. The menu is just where I keep things I mean.
Later, at Will’s table, nobody serves anybody. They pass the pan back and forth like they’ve done it for years.
ko: 오늘 밤 저녁—그리고 둘 다 이름이 있는 한 메뉴
나는 내 주머니에서 카드를 넘겨준다. 손으로 쓴: 한 6명 수프, 두 요리사들, 정가, 둘 다 이름.
es: I hand him a card from my pocket. Handwritten: a six-seat supper, two chefs, full price, both names.
I wrote us a Friday. The menu is just where I keep things I mean.
Later, at Will’s table, nobody serves anybody. They pass the pan back and forth like they’ve done it for years.

mem.en: Matteo and Will had dinner at Will’s and planned a small full-price supper together, credited to both.
mem.zh: Matteo和Will在Will家共进晚餐，并计划一起办一场署两人名字的全价小型晚宴。
mem.ja: Matteo and Will had dinner at Will’s and planned a small full-price supper together, credited to both.
mem.ko: 나는 우린 한 금요일을 썼어. 메뉴는 그냥 내가 물건들을 지키는 곳이야.
mem.es: Matteo and Will had dinner at Will’s and planned a small full-price supper together, credited to both.

t.en: Stay friends—Sunday dinners, separate kitchens
t.zh: 做朋友——各守厨房，周日一起吃
t.ja: Stay friends—Sunday dinners, separate kitchens
t.ko: 나중에, 윌의 테이블에서, 아무도가 누구도 서빙하지 않는다. 그들이 팬을 뒤와 앞으로 지나간다 마치 그들이 년들을 위해 그걸 해왔던 것처럼.
t.es: Stay friends—Sunday dinners, separate kitchens

en: Your line, my counter. I don’t want either of us to give those up. But Sundays—plain food, your place or mine.
Deal. You bring the beans. I’ll bring complaints about your portions.
It becomes a thing. Sundays. Two chefs, no tickets, and a standing argument about salt.
zh: 你的出餐线，我的吧台。我不想我们谁放弃自己的那一块。但周日——吃点家常的，你家或者我家。
成交。你带豆子。我带对你份量的抱怨。
这成了惯例。每个周日。两个厨子，没有点单，外加一场永远吵不完的“盐放多少”。
ja: Your line, my counter. I don’t want either of us to give those up. But Sundays—plain food, your place or mine.
Deal. You bring the beans. I’ll bring complaints about your portions.
It becomes a thing. 日曜日s. Two chefs, no tickets, and a standing argument about salt.
ko: 마테오와 윌이 윌의 집에 저녁을 가졌다 그리고 작은 정가 저녁을 함께 계획했어, 둘 다 신용을 받았어.
너의 라인, 내 카운터. 나는 그 주는 것을 원하지 않아. 근데 일요일들—일반 음식, 너의 장소 또는 내 것.
es: Your line, my counter. I don’t want either of us to give those up. But Sundays—plain food, your place or mine.
Deal. You bring the beans. I’ll bring complaints about your portions.
It becomes a thing. Sundays. Two chefs, no tickets, and a standing argument about salt.

mem.en: Matteo and Will chose friendship: separate missions, standing Sunday dinners.
mem.zh: Matteo和Will选择了友情：各守各的使命，每周日固定一起吃饭。
mem.ja: Matteo and Will chose friendship: separate missions, standing 日曜日 dinners.
mem.ko: 좋아. 너 콩들을 가져와. 나 너의 부분에 대해 불평을 가져올 거야.
mem.es: Matteo and Will chose friendship: separate missions, standing Sunday dinners.

t.en: Own your mistakes and part as colleagues
t.zh: 各自认错，以同事身份告别
t.ja: Own your mistakes and part as colleagues
t.ko: 그건 한 것이 되어 온다. 일요일들. 두 요리사들, 표 없음, 그리고 한 소금에 대해 서 있는 싸움.
t.es: Own your mistakes and part as colleagues

en: I pushed my menu when I should have been counting. That was mine.
I promised four hundred before I checked the truck. That was mine.
They shake hands over the debrief sheet. Next year the board pairs them with other people. The stock recipe stays taped above Will’s pot.
zh: 该数份数的时候，我在推自己的菜单。这是我的错。
没核对货车就答应了四百份。这是我的错。
两人隔着复盘表握了手。第二年，理事会给他们各自配了别的搭档。那张高汤配方，还贴在Will的汤锅上方。
ja: I pushed my menu when I should have been counting. That was mine.
I promised four hundred before I checked the truck. That was mine.
They shake hands over the debrief sheet. Next year the board pairs them with other people. The stock recipe stays taped above Will’s pot.
ko: 마테오와 윌이 우정을 선택했다: 분리된 임무들, 서 있는 일요일 저녁들.
나는 밀어낸다 내 메뉴 나는 세어야 했을 때. 그건 내 것이었다.
es: I pushed my menu when I should have been counting. That was mine.
I promised four hundred before I checked the truck. That was mine.
They shake hands over the debrief sheet. Next year the board pairs them with other people. The stock recipe stays taped above Will’s pot.

mem.en: Matteo and Will each owned their mistakes and parted as colleagues, without romance.
mem.zh: Matteo和Will各自承认了失误，以同事身份告别，没有发展恋情。
mem.ja: Matteo and Will each owned their mistakes and parted as colleagues, without romance.
mem.ko: 나는 약속했다 400 전에 나는 트럭을 확인했다. 그건 내 것이었다.
mem.es: Matteo and Will each owned their mistakes and parted as colleagues, without romance.

t.en: Both Names on the Card
t.zh: 卡片上的两个名字
t.ja: Both Names on the Card
t.ko: 그들이 토론 시트 위에 손가락을 잔다. 다음 해 보드가 그들을 다른 사람들과 짝짓는다. 재고 조리법이 윌의 냄비 위에 테이핑된 채로 있다.
t.es: Both Names on the Card

txt.en: Matteo and Will share a Friday dinner where nobody serves, then plan a small supper together—priced on quality, not sympathy. The last plate becomes their first menu.
txt.zh: Matteo和Will吃了一顿谁都不用上菜的周五晚饭，接着一起筹备了一场小型晚宴——靠真实品质定价，而不是靠同情。最后那一盘，成了他们的第一份菜单。
txt.ja: Matteo and Will share a Friday dinner where nobody serves, then plan a small supper together—priced on quality, not sympathy. The last plate becomes their first menu.
txt.ko: 마테오와 윌이 각각 그들의 실수를 소유했고 동료들로 떠났다, 로맨스 없음.
txt.es: Matteo and Will share a Friday dinner where nobody serves, then plan a small supper together—priced on quality, not sympathy. The last plate becomes their first menu.

line.en: Next time I save a plate, I’m putting both our names on it.
line.zh: 下次我再留一盘，就写上我们俩的名字。
line.ja: Next time I save a plate, I’m putting both our names on it.
line.es: Next time I save a plate, I’m putting both our names on it.

t.en: Sundays, No Tickets
t.zh: 周日，不点单
t.ja: 日曜日s, No Tickets
t.ko: 마테오와 윌이 한 금요일 저녁을 나누는데 아무도가 서빙하지 않고, 그럼 한 작은 저녁을 함께 계획해—가격은 질에, 동정이 아님. 마지막 접시가 그들의 첫 메뉴가 된다.
t.es: Sundays, No Tickets

txt.en: They respect that their work serves different people, and keep it that way. Sunday dinners become a standing date between friends—plain food, loud opinions, and a door left open.
txt.zh: 他们尊重彼此的工作服务着不同的人，也就这样守着。周日晚饭成了朋友之间的固定约会——家常菜，大嗓门的意见，还有一扇没关上的门。
txt.ja: They respect that their work serves different people, and keep it that way. Sunday dinners become a standing date between friends—plain food, loud opinions, and a door left open.
txt.ko: 다음 번 나는 한 접시를 구하면, 나는 둘 다 우리 이름을 그 위에 놓고 있어.
txt.es: They respect that their work serves different people, and keep it that way. Sunday dinners become a standing date between friends—plain food, loud opinions, and a door left open.

line.en: Your line, my counter, our Sundays.
line.zh: 你的出餐线，我的吧台，我们的周日。
line.ja: Your line, my counter, our 日曜日s.
line.es: Your line, my counter, our Sundays.

t.en: Two Kitchens
t.zh: 两间厨房
t.ja: Two Kitchens
t.ko: 그들이 존경하는 그들의 일이 다른 사람들을 제공한다, 그리고 그걸 그 방식으로 유지한다. 일요일 저녁들이 친구들 사이에 한 서 있는 날짜가 되어 온다—일반 음식, 크게 의견, 그리고 열린 한 문.
t.es: Two Kitchens

txt.en: Competition got louder than the service, and they both know it. They own their mistakes, finish the job, and go back to separate kitchens with respect intact.
txt.zh: 较劲的声音盖过了服务的初心，两人心里都清楚。他们各自认错，把活干完，带着完好的尊重回到各自的厨房。
txt.ja: Competition got louder than the service, and they both know it. They own their mistakes, finish the job, and go back to separate kitchens with respect intact.
txt.ko: 너의 라인, 내 카운터, 우리의 일요일들.
txt.es: Competition got louder than the service, and they both know it. They own their mistakes, finish the job, and go back to separate kitchens with respect intact.

line.en: We fed them. That was the job. Take care of yourself, Matteo.
line.zh: 我们让他们吃饱了。这是本分。照顾好自己，Matteo。
line.ja: We fed them. That was the job. 取る care of yourself, Matteo.
line.es: We fed them. That was the job. Take care of yourself, Matteo.

t.en: An Ordinary Weeknight
t.zh: 一个普通的工作日晚上
t.ja: An Ordinary Weeknight
t.ko: 경쟁이 서비스보다 더 시끄러워졌고, 그들 둘 다 그걸 안다. 그들이 그들의 실수를 소유하고, 일을 마치고, 분리된 부엌들 위로 존경으로 돌아간다.
t.es: An Ordinary Weeknight

d.en: On a shared day off, Matteo and Will cook each other the plainest food they know—his grandmother’s beans, Will’s boxed mac with hot sauce—and have to eat it without critiquing. Two new scenes; one of them cracks.
d.zh: 某个两人都休息的日子，Matteo和Will互相做自己会的最家常的菜——他外婆的豆子，Will的盒装芝士通心粉加辣酱——而且吃的时候不许点评。两场全新剧情；其中一个人会先破功。
d.ja: On a shared day off, Matteo and Will cook each other the plainest food they know—his grandmother’s beans, Will’s boxed mac with hot sauce—and have to eat it without critiquing. Two new scenes; one of them cracks.
d.ko: 우릴 먹였다. 그건 일이었다. 너 너 자신을 돌봐, 마테오.
d.es: On a shared day off, Matteo and Will cook each other the plainest food they know—his grandmother’s beans, Will’s boxed mac with hot sauce—and have to eat it without critiquing. Two new scenes; one of them cracks.

polaroid.en: The last plate with two forks—your caption on the border.
polaroid.zh: 最后一盘和两把叉子——在相框边写下你的题字。
polaroid.ja: The last plate with two forks—your caption on the border.
polaroid.es: The last plate with two forks—your caption on the border.

game.en: Portion planner: split real ingredients across pans and plates. The count decides who eats well—not luck.
game.zh: 份量规划：把真实的食材分配到每一锅、每一盘。能让多少人吃好，由数字决定，不靠运气。
game.ja: Portion planner: split real ingredients across pans and plates. The count decides who eats well—not luck.
game.ko: 한 모든 하루 동안 오프, 마테오와 윌이 서로 알고 있는 가장 일반한 음식을 요리하고—그의 할머니의 콩들, 윌의 상자 맥과 핫소스—그리고 비판하지 않고 그걸 먹어야 한다. 두 새로운 장면; 그들 중 한 명이 깨져 있다.
game.es: Portion planner: split real ingredients across pans and plates. The count decides who eats well—not luck.

gift.en: A handwritten menu card, or a fork of your choosing (free).
gift.zh: 一张手写菜单卡，或一把你自选的叉子（免费）。
gift.ja: A handwritten menu card, or a fork of your choosing (free).
gift.ko: 두 포크를 가진 마지막 접시—너의 캡션이 있는 테두리.
gift.es: A handwritten menu card, or a fork of your choosing (free).

date.en: A weeknight dinner where neither of them serves anybody.
date.zh: 一顿谁都不用给别人上菜的工作日晚饭。
date.ja: A weeknight dinner where neither of them serves anybody.
date.ko: 일부 계획기: 분할 진짜 재료들 여러 팬들과 접시들을 가로질러. 수가 누가 잘 먹는다—운이 아니라.
date.es: A weeknight dinner where neither of them serves anybody.

photo.en: Tiny bite vs. hotel pan, the scrap-stock soup, the second fork.
photo.zh: 一口小菜对大餐盘、边角料熬的热汤、第二把叉。
photo.ja: Tiny bite vs. hotel pan, the scrap-stock soup, the second fork.
photo.ko: 한 손으로 쓴 메뉴 카드, 또는 너의 선택하는 포크 (자유).
photo.es: Tiny bite vs. hotel pan, the scrap-stock soup, the second fork.

voice.en: Will’s supper invitation, and Matteo’s voicemail reading out a menu of plain food.
voice.zh: Will的晚餐邀请，以及Matteo留言念出的一份家常菜单。
voice.ja: Will’s supper invitation, and Matteo’s voicemail reading out a menu of plain food.
voice.ko: 한 주중날 저녁 어디 아무도가 누구도 서빙하지 않는다.
voice.es: Will’s supper invitation, and Matteo’s voicemail reading out a menu of plain food.

room.en: The second fork and the shared menu, framed.
room.zh: 第二把叉，和装进相框的共同菜单。
room.ja: The second fork and the shared menu, framed.
room.ko: 작은 입맛 vs. 호텔 팬, 부스러기-재고 수프, 두 번째 포크.
room.es: The second fork and the shared menu, framed.

allowed.en: Change the portion count and watch the consequences change with it
allowed.zh: 调整份数，看后果随之变化
allowed.ja: Change the portion count and watch the consequences change with it
allowed.ko: 윌의 저녁 초대, 그리고 마테오의 음성 메일 일반 음식의 메뉴를 읽는다.
allowed.es: Change the portion count and watch the consequences change with it

allowed.en: Move the supper to another night—check both chefs’ schedules first
allowed.zh: 把晚餐挪到别的晚上——先核对两位主厨的时间
allowed.ja: Move the supper to another night—check both chefs’ schedules first
allowed.ko: 두 번째 포크와 공유 메뉴, 틀 지어져.
allowed.es: Move the supper to another night—check both chefs’ schedules first

allowed.en: Add a third person (a volunteer, a critic) with a clear role and what they know
allowed.zh: 加入第三个人（志愿者或评论家），需交代身份、来由和所知范围
allowed.ja: Add a third person (a volunteer, a critic) with a clear role and what they know
allowed.ko: 일부 수를 바꿔 그리고 대체도를 따라봐 바뀌는 것.
allowed.es: Add a third person (a volunteer, a critic) with a clear role and what they know

au.en: AU: a regular full-price tasting dinner, no benefit
au.zh: AU：一场普通的收费试餐，不是公益活动
au.ja: AU: a regular full-price tasting dinner, no benefit
au.ko: 저녁을 다른 밤으로 옮겨라—둘 다 요리사들의 일정을 먼저 체크해
au.es: AU: a regular full-price tasting dinner, no benefit

au.en: AU: they start as friends before any supper
au.zh: AU：在任何晚餐之前，他们先是朋友
au.ja: AU: they start as friends before any supper
au.ko: 한 세 번째 사람 추가 (한 자원 봉사자, 한 비평가) 명확한 역할과 그들이 알았던 것
au.es: AU: they start as friends before any supper
